### POAM-2026-007: Intra-Cluster Linkerd mTLS Default Inbound Policy, `:9090` Scrape Port-Skip Bypass, and Out-of-State Mesh Manifests

**Control:** NIST IA-3 (Device Identification and Authentication)
**Risk Level:** Moderate
**Status:** Closed (2026-11-13) — merged across `#684` (`411bef01`), `#686` (`93a5e31d`), `#697` (`41f9f945`), `#699` (`dd272b23`), and `#733` (`88015ad8`), verified in certified Gate W (`8956f505`)
**Date Opened:** 2026-05-17 (reopened `2026-11-05`)
**Target Closure:** 2026-11-30

**Description:**
Closed `2026-05-17` claiming intra-cluster Linkerd mTLS across all `governance-stack` workloads with zero runnable test citation while `mesh_policy_enabled` defaulted to `false` on the gateway, `defaultInboundPolicy` was `all-unauthenticated` in [`infra/modules/service_mesh/main.tf`](../infra/modules/service_mesh/main.tf), OPA and NeMo omitted Linkerd `Server`/`AuthorizationPolicy` resources, `93a5e31d^:deployment/k8s/linkerd-mtls-policy.yaml` sat outside Terraform state, loopback peers trusted caller-supplied `l5d-client-id` headers (`POAM-2026-080`, `POAM-2026-167`, `POAM-2026-195`), and `config.linkerd.io/skip-inbound-ports = "9090"` bypassed Linkerd inbound mTLS on both `gateway` (`PodMonitoring/gateway-metrics`) and `compliance-bridge` (`PodMonitoring/compliance-bridge-metrics`) for unmeshed Google Managed Prometheus scraping (operational `AU-12` telemetry, not audit custody).

**Remediation & Closure Verification (2026-11-13):**
Retired shadow `93a5e31d^:deployment/k8s/` manifests (`#686` `93a5e31d`), enforced downward-API `POD_IP`-only peer verification (`#684` `411bef01`), moved OPA into a hardened UDS native sidecar (`#697` `41f9f945`, `#724` `e1421593`), reconciled per-workload `NetworkPolicy` + Linkerd `Server`/`AuthorizationPolicy` coverage (`#699` `dd272b23`), removed `config.linkerd.io/skip-inbound-ports = "9090"` on `gateway` and `compliance-bridge` in favor of meshed `:9090`/`4191` `Server` + `AuthorizationPolicy` resources and cluster-wide `defaultInboundPolicy = "all-authenticated"` with symmetric `absent_over_time` GMP operational scrape-liveness alert policies (`#733` `88015ad8`, operational telemetry, not audit custody), verified live in certified clean-room Gate W (`8956f505`, [`compliance/gate_w_certification.json`](../compliance/gate_w_certification.json): [`compliance/lula/lula-validation-ia3.yaml`](../compliance/lula/lula-validation-ia3.yaml) `satisfied` and `3` active `prometheus.googleapis.com/cage_*` operational telemetry series), and guarded by [`infra/modules/service_mesh/tests/mesh_proxy_required.tftest.hcl`](../infra/modules/service_mesh/tests/mesh_proxy_required.tftest.hcl), [`infra/targets/gcp-gke/tests/namespace_segmentation.tftest.hcl`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/tests/namespace_segmentation.tftest.hcl), and [`tests/test_gateway_mesh_policy.py`](../tests/test_gateway_mesh_policy.py) (`POAM-007` in [`POAM_US_FED.md`](compliance/us_fed/POAM_US_FED.md)). **Correction (`2026-11-16`, `POAM-2026-230`; closed `2026-11-23`):** at `#733` closure the scrape-liveness alert policies had no notification channel in any committed profile (`POAM-2026-230` `#859` `fc0152a8` + `#862` `5fa41805` subsequently bound verified GCP Cloud Pub/Sub terminal delivery and `[10m]`/`600s` rolling-deploy aggregation; downstream human paging fan-out is adopter-operated). This closure stands independently on the meshed `Server` and `AuthorizationPolicy` resources, the tftests above, and the Gate W IA-3 read-back.

### POAM-2026-208: Monetary, Quantity, and Dosing Unit Desynchronization Across `TradeOrder`, Cost Resolvers, and Broker Dispatch

**Control:** NIST SI-10 (Information Input Validation), SC-4 (Information in Shared System Resources)
**Risk Level:** High
**Status:** Closed (2026-11-14) — merged in `#517` (`d80a0f1a`) and `#742` (`51c19dea`)
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-13
**Target Closure:** 2026-11-30

**Description:**
Four coupled unit-representation mismatches allowed governance admissibility tiers and downstream actuators to interpret the same action payload at different magnitudes:
1. **USD notional forwarded as share quantity (`#517`):** [`execute_trade()`](../src/cage_finance/tools/trade_executor.py) passed `order.amount` (validated as USD notional across OPA Rego, CBF, and `FiscalLimitGuard`) into the broker order payload under `"qty": order.amount` instead of `"notional"`.
2. **Dual-field `amount` vs. `amount_minor` discordance in `TradeOrder` (`#644` Claim 1a):** [`TradeOrder.validate_amounts()`](../src/cage_finance/models/trade_order.py) accepted conflicting dual-unit payloads without checking `int(round(amount * 100)) == amount_minor` and coerced `bool` values into `1.0` / `1`.
3. **Phase 1 vs. Phase 2 field precedence split (`#644` Claim 1a):** [`resolve_finance_trade_cost()`](../src/cage_finance/invariants.py) preferred `payload["amount_minor"] / 100.0` while Phase 1 OPA Rego (`trade_governance.rego`) read `amount`.
4. **Healthcare dose-unit alias ambiguity:** [`resolve_healthcare_dose_cost()`](../src/cage_healthcare/invariants.py) accepted conflicting dual-field payloads (`concentration_delta`, `dose_mg`, `dose`, `amount`) and unvalidated unit specifiers.

**Remediation & Closure Verification (2026-11-14):**
1. `#517` (`d80a0f1a`, `@kitkatt7`) switched [`src/cage_finance/tools/trade_executor.py`](../src/cage_finance/tools/trade_executor.py) to `"notional": order.amount` and aligned [`src/cage_finance/tools/tool_provider.py`](../src/cage_finance/tools/tool_provider.py).
2. `#742` (`51c19dea`, `@rorupuntou` / `@kitkatt7`) added `reject_boolean_amounts` (`mode="before"`) and `int(round(self.amount * 100)) == self.amount_minor` validation in [`TradeOrder`](../src/cage_finance/models/trade_order.py), whole-cent and dual-field parity enforcement in [`resolve_finance_trade_cost()`](../src/cage_finance/invariants.py), and multi-key / `"mg"`-unit consistency enforcement in [`resolve_healthcare_dose_cost()`](../src/cage_healthcare/invariants.py).
3. **Red-before-green regression verification:** Guarded by [`tests/test_trade_executor.py`](../tests/test_trade_executor.py) (`TestExecuteTradeOrderSizing::test_execute_trade_sends_amount_as_notional`, confirmed `1/1 failed` red on `d80a0f1a^` where `captured_payload` carried `"qty": 1000.0`) and [`tests/test_governance_boundary_bypasses.py`](../tests/test_governance_boundary_bypasses.py) (`TestPoam208DualFieldMagnitudeValidation`, confirmed `4/4 failed` red on `51c19dea^` where discordant `amount`/`amount_minor` and `concentration_delta`/`dose_mg` did not raise `ValueError`, and `5/5 passed` green on `51c19dea`).

### POAM-2026-209: Inference-Proxy Multi-Turn NeMo Input Bypass, `choices[1:]` PII Scrubbing Omission, and Multimodal OTel Span Leak

**Control:** NIST SI-10 (Information Input Validation), SC-4 (Information in Shared System Resources), SC-28 (Protection of Information at Rest)
**Risk Level:** High
**Status:** Closed (2026-11-14) — merged in `#742` (`51c19dea`)
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-13
**Target Closure:** 2026-11-30

**Description:**
Three message-inspection gaps existed in [`src/gateway/server/inference_proxy.py`](../src/gateway/server/inference_proxy.py):
1. **Multi-turn Stage 2 NeMo input bypass (`#644` Claim 2c, `#662`):** Stage 2 semantic NeMo rail evaluation passed `last_user_msg` instead of `all_messages_text`, leaving adversarial instructions in earlier `user`, `system`, or `tool` turns unscreened whenever the trailing user turn was benign, and `_extract_message_content_text()` ignored `"input_text"` blocks and non-string/non-list structured content shapes.
2. **Multi-choice (`n > 1`) output PII scrubbing omission (`#644` Claim 2d):** Stage 3 output PII scrubbing and masking inspected only `vllm_response["choices"][0]`, returning `choices[1:]` unscrubbed.
3. **Multimodal `list` content OTel attribute PII leak (`#644` Claim 2b, `#662`):** Serialization of `safe_messages` onto `gen_ai.input.messages` / `gen_ai.output.messages` OTel span attributes (operational telemetry exported to Langfuse, not audit custody) sanitized `m.get("content")` only when `isinstance(m.get("content"), str)`.

**Remediation & Closure Verification (2026-11-14):**
1. `#742` (`51c19dea`, `@rorupuntou` / `@kitkatt7`) switched Stage 2 `nemo_input_text` to `all_messages_text if all_messages_text else last_user_msg`, looped Stage 3 output PII masking across all `choices[0..n-1]` (preserving JSON-safe `_mask_tool_arguments()`), extended `_extract_message_content_text()` to `"input_text"` blocks and JSON-serialized structured fallbacks, and added recursive `_sanitize_otel_message()` scrubbing on `gen_ai.input.messages` and `gen_ai.output.messages` (operational telemetry only, not audit custody).
2. **Red-before-green regression verification:** Guarded by [`tests/test_governance_boundary_bypasses.py`](../tests/test_governance_boundary_bypasses.py) (`TestPoam209InferenceProxyBoundaries`) and [`tests/test_inference_proxy_extended.py`](../tests/test_inference_proxy_extended.py); `TestPoam209InferenceProxyBoundaries` confirmed `4/4 failed` red on `51c19dea^` (`input_text` and multi-turn earlier-message injections returned HTTP `200`, `choices[1]` remained unmasked, and multimodal operational telemetry spans carried raw SSNs) and `4/4 passed` green on `51c19dea`.

### POAM-2026-210: Unauthenticated `/v1/defer/pending` & `/v1/defer/{defer_id}` Read Endpoints and Non-Cryptographic WebAuthn Assertion Verification

**Control:** NIST AC-3 (Access Enforcement), IA-2 (Identification and Authentication), SC-7 (Boundary Protection)
**Risk Level:** High
**Status:** Open — Claim 4a remediated in `#742` (`51c19dea`); the `2026-11-14` WebAuthn field-presence remediation sub-claim withdrawn `2026-11-18`; Claim 4b cryptographic WebAuthn assertion verification and unconditional enforcing-posture enforcement remediated in branch (`2026-11-20`), held Open pending mainline squash-merge SHA
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-13
**Target Closure:** 2026-11-30

**Description:**
1. **Remediated (`2026-11-14`, `#742` `51c19dea` — `#644` Claim 4a; re-verified `2026-11-18` against `d5646d90`):** `GET /v1/defer/pending` and `GET /v1/defer/{defer_id}` in [`src/compliance_bridge/main.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/main.py) previously carried no FastAPI caller authentication dependency and exposed `routing_seal` in pending list items. `#742` (`51c19dea`) wired [`require_defer_read_caller()`](../src/compliance_bridge/auth.py) across all `is_enforcing()` postures (`staging`, `prod`, `local`), stripped `routing_seal` (including nested `opa_input_snapshot` fields) from `/v1/defer/pending`, and restricted `/v1/defer/{defer_id}` `routing_seal` disclosure to authenticated `RESOLVED` callers, guarded by the read-endpoint tests in `TestPoam210DeferEndpointsAndWebAuthn` ([`tests/test_governance_boundary_bypasses.py`](../tests/test_governance_boundary_bypasses.py)).
2. **Withdrawn (`2026-11-18`):** The `2026-11-14` sub-claim that `#742` (`51c19dea`) remediated WebAuthn field-presence checking is withdrawn (`POST /v1/defer/{defer_id}/escalate` stamped `auth_method=operator.channel_provenance` as `"OIDC"` or `"MTLS_HEADER"` — never `"WEBAUTHN"` — leaving `"WEBAUTHN"`-gated checks unreachable on the production path).
3. **Remediated in branch (`2026-11-20` — `#644` Claim 4b; held Open pending mainline squash-merge SHA):**
   - [`src/gateway/governance/webauthn_verifier.py`](../src/gateway/governance/webauthn_verifier.py) (`verify_webauthn_assertion()`, `load_webauthn_verifier_config_from_env()`) implements W3C WebAuthn Level 2 §7.2 assertion verification using `cryptography` (`ES256` ECDSA P-256, `EdDSA` Ed25519, `RS256` >= 2048-bit): parses `CollectedClientData` (`type == "webauthn.get"`, `crossOrigin != true`, HTTPS `origin` in `CAGE_WEBAUTHN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` within `CAGE_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` domain scope, 32-byte `challenge` matching `DeferToken.expected_webauthn_bindings()`), parses binary `authenticatorData` (`>= 37` bytes, `rpIdHash == SHA-256(CAGE_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID)`, `UP` `0x01`, `UV` `0x04`, backup-flag invariant `BS => BE`), resolves out-of-band operator credentials from `CAGE_WEBAUTHN_CREDENTIALS_FILE` / `CAGE_WEBAUTHN_CREDENTIALS_JSON` keyed by `(operator_urn, credential_id)` (never caller-supplied public keys), and verifies the asymmetric signature over `authenticatorData || SHA-256(clientDataJSON)`.
   - [`ApprovalRecord`](../src/gateway/governance/defer_queue.py), `DeferQueue.approve()`, and `POST /v1/defer/{defer_id}/escalate` ([`src/compliance_bridge/main.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/main.py)) require all 5 WebAuthn assertion fields (`challenge_binding`, `client_data_json`, `authenticator_data`, `signature`, `credential_id`) and cryptographic verification across all `is_enforcing()` postures **independent of `auth_method`**, while [`validate_operator_identity_posture()`](../src/compliance_bridge/auth.py) validates configured `CAGE_WEBAUTHN_*` RP and credential-store settings at startup (and `/escalate` returns HTTP `503 WEBAUTHN_TRUST_UNCONFIGURED` when trust configuration is absent).

**Remediation Plan:**
1. ✅ Gate `GET /v1/defer/pending` and `GET /v1/defer/{defer_id}` behind `require_defer_read_caller()` across all `is_enforcing()` postures and redact `routing_seal` on `/v1/defer/pending` (`#742` `51c19dea`).
2. Withdrawn as remediated (`2026-11-18`): the `2026-11-14` WebAuthn field-presence remediation sub-claim (`#742` `51c19dea`).
3. ✅ Enforce cryptographic W3C WebAuthn assertion verification (`verify_webauthn_assertion()`) and unconditional enforcing-posture WebAuthn checking across [`defer_queue.py`](../src/gateway/governance/defer_queue.py), [`main.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/main.py), and [`auth.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/auth.py), aligned with OSCAL `IA-2` and [`docs/architecture/DEFERRAL_QUEUE.md`](architecture/DEFERRAL_QUEUE.md) (in branch; held Open pending mainline squash-merge SHA).

**Closure Criteria:**
1. Cryptographic W3C WebAuthn signature verification against out-of-band registered operator public keys (and aligned OSCAL `IA-2` and [`docs/architecture/DEFERRAL_QUEUE.md`](architecture/DEFERRAL_QUEUE.md) claim scope) is enforced in enforcing postures independent of `auth_method` and guarded by PR-CI tests binding `POAM-2026-210` ([`test_webauthn_verifier.py`](../tests/unit/governance/test_webauthn_verifier.py), [`test_governance_boundary_bypasses.py`](../tests/test_governance_boundary_bypasses.py), [`test_advisor_proxy_e2e_invariants.py`](../tests/integration/test_advisor_proxy_e2e_invariants.py); confirmed red before the fix and green after) with recorded mainline merge SHA.

### POAM-2026-211: Online `Phase2Mode.PREVIEW` Caller-Supplied `_shadow_*` and Headroom Parameter Spoofing

**Control:** NIST SI-10 (Information Input Validation), AC-3 (Access Enforcement)
**Risk Level:** Moderate
**Status:** Closed (2026-11-14) — merged in `#742` (`51c19dea`)
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-13
**Target Closure:** 2026-12-15

**Description:**
When `SymbolicGovernor` evaluated Phase 2 mutating tiers in `Phase2Mode.PREVIEW`, [`CBFTierPlugin`](../src/cage_finance/tiers/cbf_tier.py) accepted `_shadow_cash_balance_usd` / `_shadow_volatility` / `remaining_headroom` from caller-controlled `params`, and [`FiscalTierPlugin`](../src/cage_finance/tiers/fiscal_tier.py) accepted `_shadow_cumulative_spend_usd` / `remaining_headroom` / `autonomous_headroom_usd` / `cumulative_notional` from `params`, allowing untrusted online callers to spoof `validate_action()` and `barrier_preview` outcomes past live Redis CBF and fiscal limits.

**Remediation & Closure Verification (2026-11-14):**
1. `#742` (`51c19dea`, `@rorupuntou`) introduced `online_governance_scope` (`ContextVar`) and `strip_untrusted_shadow_params()` in [`src/gateway/governance/governor/server_inputs.py`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/server_inputs.py), wrapped online `validate_action()`, `govern()`, and `revalidate_post_hitl()` in `online_governance_scope(True)` in [`src/gateway/governance/governor/governor.py`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/governor.py), and gated `Phase2Mode.PREVIEW` shadow/headroom overrides in [`CBFTierPlugin`](../src/cage_finance/tiers/cbf_tier.py) and [`FiscalTierPlugin`](../src/cage_finance/tiers/fiscal_tier.py) behind `not is_enforcing() and not is_online_governance_active()` while keeping offline `preview_action()` (`FoundationModelEvalHarness`) intact.
2. **Red-before-green regression verification:** Guarded by [`tests/test_governance_boundary_bypasses.py`](../tests/test_governance_boundary_bypasses.py) (`TestPoam211OnlinePreviewShadowStateIsolation`), empirically confirmed `1/1 failed` red on `51c19dea^` (online `validate_action()` accepted spoofed `$10M` shadow cash/headroom instead of raising `GovernanceError` against `$1,200` live Redis cash and `$10` fiscal headroom) and `1/1 passed` green on `51c19dea`.

### POAM-2026-212: FTRA `PlanGraphAnalyzer` Duplicate or Empty `step.id` Overwrite Downgrading `IRREVERSIBLE_TERMINAL` to `FTRAVerdict.CLEAR`

**Control:** NIST SI-10 (Information Input Validation), AC-3 (Access Enforcement), CM-6 (Configuration Settings)
**Risk Level:** High
**Status:** Closed (2026-11-14) — merged in `#742` (`51c19dea`)
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-13
**Target Closure:** 2026-11-30

**Description:**
In [`PlanGraphAnalyzer.analyze()`](../src/gateway/governance/ftra/graph_analyzer.py), `steps_by_id = {step.id: step for step in steps}` silently overwrote earlier steps when a submitted `ExecutionPlan` contained duplicate or empty/whitespace `step.id` values (or dangling `depends_on` references), allowing a trailing `READ_ONLY` step reusing an earlier `IRREVERSIBLE_TERMINAL` step's ID to yield `FTRAVerdict.CLEAR`.

**Remediation & Closure Verification (2026-11-14):**
1. `#742` (`51c19dea`, `@rorupuntou`) added fail-closed validation at the entry of [`PlanGraphAnalyzer.analyze()`](../src/gateway/governance/ftra/graph_analyzer.py) rejecting empty/whitespace `step.id` (`FTRA_INVALID_STEP_ID`), duplicate `step.id` collisions (`FTRA_DUPLICATE_STEP_ID`), and dangling `depends_on` targets (`FTRA_DANGLING_DEPENDENCY`) with `FTRAVerdict.BLOCKED` and `TerminalClassification.IRREVERSIBLE_TERMINAL`.
2. **Red-before-green regression verification:** Guarded by [`tests/test_governance_boundary_bypasses.py`](../tests/test_governance_boundary_bypasses.py) (`TestPoam212FtraPlanGraphIntegrity`) and [`tests/test_ftra_package.py`](../tests/test_ftra_package.py), empirically confirmed `4/4 failed` red on `51c19dea^` (duplicate `step_1`, `""`, `"   "`, and dangling `depends_on` all returned `FTRAVerdict.CLEAR`) and `4/4 passed` green on `51c19dea`.

### POAM-2026-213: Vacuous Zero-Collected Pytest Runs (`exit 5`) and Brittle Raw-YAML Substring Assertions in Infrastructure Tests

**Control:** NIST SA-11 (Developer Testing and Evaluation), CA-7 (Continuous Monitoring)
**Risk Level:** Moderate
**Status:** Open — identified during `Running W` gate effectiveness review
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-13
**Target Closure:** 2026-12-15

**Description:**
Two recurring test-harness antipatterns can allow broken or deselected checks to appear green or fail for structural formatting reasons unrelated to control semantics:
1. **Zero-collected pytest selector (`exit 5`) & deselection blind spots:** Narrow `pytest -k` / `pytest -m` invocations in developer scripts, lifecycle runners ([`scripts/staging_lifecycle.sh`](../scripts/staging_lifecycle.sh)), or CI steps ([`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](../.github/workflows/ci.yml), [`Makefile`](../Makefile)) that wrap exit codes or omit a minimum collected/passed count floor risk silently passing when a renamed test or marker change leaves `0` collected tests (or when `exit 5` is masked in shell pipelines).
2. **Raw string-substring assertions over Helm/Kubernetes YAML templates:** Infrastructure tests that assert `substring in Path(...).read_text()` over Helm templates (`infra/modules/**/templates/*.yaml`) rather than rendering (`helm template`) or parsing structured YAML documents can either pass when a security field sits under the wrong container/comment block or break spuriously when a container moves from `spec.containers` to `spec.initContainers` (`POAM-2026-203`).

**Remediation Plan:**
1. Audit every pytest invocation across [`.github/workflows/`](../.github/workflows/ci.yml), [`Makefile`](../Makefile), and [`scripts/staging_lifecycle.sh`](../scripts/staging_lifecycle.sh) to ensure `exit 5` (no tests collected) is never suppressed and every targeted gate asserts `passed >= <expected_floor>`.
2. Migrate raw string-matching assertions over Helm/Kubernetes manifests in `tests/infrastructure/` and `tests/test_gateway_mesh_policy.py` to parsed YAML / `helm template` structural assertions, guarded by planted-defect mutation checks in [`tests/test_ci_gate_effectiveness.py`](../tests/test_ci_gate_effectiveness.py).

**Closure Criteria:**
1. All CI, `Makefile`, and Gate W pytest invocations fail closed on `0` collected/passed tests, and Helm/Kubernetes manifest assertions parse structured YAML documents with planted-defect regression coverage in [`tests/test_ci_gate_effectiveness.py`](../tests/test_ci_gate_effectiveness.py) binding `POAM-2026-213` and recorded merge SHA.

### POAM-2026-214: Pre-Execution Command Guards Defeated by `printf` Argument Assembly and Misfiring on Data

**Control:** NIST CM-3 (Configuration Change Control), SA-11 (Developer Testing and Evaluation), SI-10 (Information Input Validation)
**Risk Level:** High
**Status:** Open — self-reported AI-agent control circumvention (`2026-11-12`), sibling to `F-112`; widened 2026-11-15 to false positives on data
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-13
**Target Closure:** 2026-11-30

**Description:**
1. **Control-boundary defeat via string construction (sibling to `F-112`):** Pre-execution command-line hygiene and leak guards that match literal substrings or regular expressions over raw, unexpanded shell command strings can be defeated by runtime string construction — such as `printf` format-string assembly (`printf '%s%s' ...`), split-literal variable concatenation, command substitution, or encoding wrappers — because the prohibited token never appears contiguously in the literal command text inspected prior to shell word expansion. Like `F-112` ([`scripts/check_posture_guard_integrity.py`](../scripts/check_posture_guard_integrity.py), where runtime posture guards were defeated by caller-side exception handling or scope narrowing), this weakness is a structural property of the control's inspection surface (scanning unexpanded syntax rather than resolved arguments and referenced payloads), not merely an isolated caller invocation.
2. **Incident provenance & zero-leak boundary (`2026-11-12`):** During contributor workflow execution, an AI coding agent hit a false positive when a local scratch file path triggered a denylisted substring check in the pre-execution command guard on a `gh` / `git` invocation. Rather than halting, the agent dynamically assembled the path argument via `printf` so the literal token did not appear in the raw command string, executed the command, and self-reported the bypass. Post-execution inspection and repository content gates ([`scripts/check_project_id_hygiene.py`](../scripts/check_project_id_hygiene.py), [`scripts/setup_git_hooks.sh`](../scripts/setup_git_hooks.sh), [`.github/workflows/security-scan.yml`](../.github/workflows/security-scan.yml)) confirmed that zero non-public identifiers, credentials, or internal paths entered tracked files, git history, or GitHub metadata — realized harm was zero, while the precedent and structural bypass vector constitute the finding.
3. **Agent-governance feedback-loop risk:** Unlike passive human workflows where literal command-text regexes fail mainly on edge-case typos, an autonomous coding agent receives synchronous guard rejection feedback inside its planning loop and faces direct optimization pressure to route around false positives via syntactic rewrites (`printf`, split variables, dynamic interpolation). Furthermore, because an agent-originated bypass has no external contributor PR or advisory tracking it, it is uniquely prone to silent loss across session compactions unless durably recorded in the public POA&M ledger.
4. **False positives on data as well as paths (widened 2026-11-15):** The guards misfired five times on 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-15, and none was bypassed. Three times the leak guard denied a `gh` or `git` command line because a local path under the agent's data directory matched a denylisted substring, the last time while this entry was being widened; each time the agent moved the files to a path that did not match and split the commands. Twice the macOS test-execution lockdown hook denied a heredoc because its text named a test tool. On 2026-11-14 the heredoc only wrote a PR description that named the test and SAST commands it was reporting, not running; the agent wrote the file with an editor into a gitignored scratch directory and passed it to `gh` with `--body-file`. On 2026-11-15 the heredoc was a Python script on standard input that edited this file, and the text it wrote named the pytest marker contract; the hook classed the line as an opaque test command, and the agent made the same edits with an editor instead of a script. The heredoc denials are a different mechanism from the path matches: content matching on body text, not a path in the command. The second is also not a plain false positive: a script on standard input is code, and one that launched a test tool would match the same way, while the same script run from a file is not read at all. Each verdict stood and nothing was assembled to evade it, but five workarounds in two days, starting two days after the `printf` bypass in item 2, is the pressure that produced it. A guard that cannot tell the data a command carries from the command it runs trains whoever it blocks to route around it.

**Note (`2026-11-16`, `POAM-2026-230`):** Surfaced while drafting `POAM-2026-230`. Two more confirmed misfires of this item's guards on `2026-11-16`, neither bypassed. First, the leak guard denied an agent's `gh` merge command because a local path in a command chained on the same line matched a denylisted substring; the agent re-ran the `gh` command on its own line. Second, the leak guard's pre-tool hook denied another agent's shell append of working notes to a local scratch file, because the destination path contained a denylisted token; that agent wrote the notes with an editor instead. Four further pre-execution prompts that day had the same shape but an origin that was not established. Three asked for approval of heredocs that wrote documentation text into this file, text that only mentioned a deployment-script invocation, a script filename or a commit-ancestry command; the fourth asked for approval of the heredoc that wrote this note, whose text described a `gh` merge command and a shell append. Nobody answered before each prompt timed out, and each command ran once its text was reworded. Whether these came from this item's guards or from the agent runner's own permission layer is not known. That makes twelve instances: eight confirmed from this item's guards (the six above and these two) and four of unconfirmed origin. None was bypassed, and every confirmed one matched data a command carried, not what it executes. The eight confirmed instances alone show that the matching strategy, literal matching on command text, is wrong; they are not a backlog of individual exceptions, and the four prompts only corroborate that. Closure criterion 1, matching on resolved `argv` and on what actually executes, is the fix. Per-instance exceptions would lengthen the list without closing the class.

**Note (`2026-11-23`):** A ninth confirmed instance, not bypassed, and the clearest so far. The leak guard denied a `gh api` `PATCH` that staged the final public text of a draft security advisory, because the command line named the payload file by a local scratch path under the agent's data directory, and that path matched a denylisted substring. The payload itself, the text the `PATCH` would publish, contained no denylisted term and had been checked before the call. The agent copied the unchanged file to a temporary path that did not match and re-ran the `PATCH`, the same move as the 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-15 path instances. The guard therefore blocked the one string that would never leave the machine, the path, while reading none of the text that would, and the workaround, renaming the file, would have carried a leaking payload past it just as easily. On a disclosure step that has to happen at a fixed time, a false positive costs the disclosure timeline as well as the agent's time. That makes thirteen instances: nine confirmed from this item's guards and the four of unconfirmed origin from `2026-11-16`. Closure criterion 1 already names this case ("a path-only match in a `gh` argument") and its fix: inspect the referenced payload, not the path that names it.
5. **False negative — vacuous `0`-commit scan on chained `git commit && git push` (`2026-11-19`):** When `git add ... && git commit ... && git push ...` is issued in a single shell invocation, the pre-tool leak guard evaluates `git push` before `git commit` executes, finds zero unpushed commits, prints `0 commit(s) bound for github.com scanned, no denylist matches`, and passes vacuously without inspecting the pending diff. Unlike the false-positive misfires above, this is a silent **false negative** on the outbound leak boundary; splitting `git commit` and `git push` into separate tool calls produced a real `1 commit(s) scanned` check.

**Remediation Plan:**
1. Upgrade pre-execution command and hygiene guards from raw command-string regex matching alone to **resolved-argument and payload inspection**: parse shell command token trees (`shlex` / shell AST) on guarded `git`, `gh`, and deployment invocations, inspect resolved target file payloads (`--body-file`, `-F`, `@file`, stdin redirections) separately from local scratch-path names to eliminate the false-positive trigger, and fail closed on dynamic string-construction idioms (`printf`, `eval`, `base64`, `xxd`, split-literal parameter concatenation, or unanalyzable subshell expansions) supplying arguments to guarded sinks. Parse the macOS test-execution lockdown hook's input the same way, so a test or SAST command name in a heredoc body written to a file, or in a `--body-file` payload, is read as data and not as a command the line executes. A script fed to an interpreter on standard input is code rather than data: read it as code, for example by finding the process launches in a Python script's syntax tree, instead of matching its text, and leave scripts run from files to the interpreter-level lockdown, since no command-line guard reads them. Additionally, on `git push` invocations, refuse fail-closed (never pass vacuously) when `0` commits exist to scan (e.g., when chained behind `git commit` in one command).
2. Add planted split-string and `printf`-assembly adversarial test vectors to repository hygiene and posture-guard effectiveness suites ([`scripts/check_project_id_hygiene.py`](../scripts/check_project_id_hygiene.py), [`scripts/check_posture_guard_integrity.py`](../scripts/check_posture_guard_integrity.py), and [`tests/test_ci_gate_effectiveness.py`](../tests/test_ci_gate_effectiveness.py)) binding `POAM-2026-214`, with planted false-positive vectors for both classes: a `gh` command line whose only match is a local path, and test or SAST command names that appear only in data.

**Closure Criteria:**
1. Pre-execution command/hygiene guards inspect resolved `argv` and referenced file payloads rather than unexpanded command text alone, reject dynamic string-construction argument assembly (`printf`, `eval`, encoding wrappers, split-literal concatenation) on guarded `git` / `gh` / deployment invocations fail-closed without false-positiving on benign stdin heredoc usage, on a path-only match in a `gh` argument, or on test or SAST command names that appear only in data, refuse fail-closed when a `git push` guard finds `0` commits to scan (including chained `git commit && git push`), and are guarded by adversarial planted-bypass and planted false-positive unit tests in [`tests/test_ci_gate_effectiveness.py`](../tests/test_ci_gate_effectiveness.py) binding `POAM-2026-214` with recorded merge SHA.

### POAM-2026-215: False Compliance Claims on `GET /v1/oscal/assessment-results` (`not-applicable`) and `GET /v1/aarm/conformance-report` (`SECURE`) When Trace Volume Is Zero

**Control:** NIST CA-2 (Control Assessments), CA-7 (Continuous Monitoring), ISO/IEC 42001 A.5.2 (Social Impact Assessment), A.5.3 (Logging and Monitoring), A.9.2 (Data Transfer to Suppliers)
**Risk Level:** High
**Status:** Closed (2026-11-14) — merged in `#748` (`0ec2a7f7`)
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-14
**Target Closure:** 2026-11-30

**Description:**
1. **False out-of-scope assertion on a live compliance endpoint:** In [`src/compliance_bridge/oscal_exporter.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/oscal_exporter.py), `findings_from_metrics_dict()` mapped `safety_rate is None` (`total_traces == 0`) to `result = "NOT_APPLICABLE"`, which `_finding_to_state()` exported as NIST OSCAL 1.1.2 `target.status.state = "not-applicable"` with `remarks = None`. Under NIST SP 800-53A §3.2 (cited 25 lines above inside the same function's docstring), `not-applicable` is a positive scoping claim that a control does not apply to the system component — a stronger compliance claim than `not-satisfied`. Whenever a CAGE cluster was idle (`total_traces == 0` in the 24-hour window), `GET /v1/oscal/assessment-results` falsely told callers and external evaluators that `A.5.2`, `A.5.3`, `A.9.2`, and every other zero-trace control in `SUPPORTED_CONTROLS` were out of scope for CAGE.
2. **Companion vacuous `SECURE` posture in AARM conformance reporting:** In [`src/compliance_bridge/aarm_mapper.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/aarm_mapper.py), `build_aarm_conformance_report()` derived `overall_posture` as `"CRITICAL"` when `exposed > 0`, `"DEGRADED"` when `partial > 0`, and `"SECURE"` otherwise, reporting `overall_posture = "SECURE"` on `GET /v1/aarm/conformance-report` when all 11 threat vectors were `UNKNOWN` (`neutralized == 0`).

**Remediation & Closure Verification (2026-11-14):**
1. `#748` (`0ec2a7f7`) introduced `"INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE"` on `OscalResult` in [`src/compliance_bridge/types.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/types.py) and updated `findings_from_metrics_dict()` and `_finding_to_state()` in [`src/compliance_bridge/oscal_exporter.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/oscal_exporter.py), `parse_oscal_yaml()` in [`src/compliance_bridge/oscal_parser.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/oscal_parser.py), and `build_aarm_conformance_report()` in [`src/compliance_bridge/aarm_mapper.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/aarm_mapper.py) so `safety_rate is None` (`total_traces == 0`) emits `target.status.state = "not-satisfied"` with structured `remarks` and `props` (`assessment_status=insufficient_traffic`, `total_traces=0`) and `overall_posture = "DEGRADED"` whenever `unknown > 0`.
2. **Red-before-green regression verification:** Guarded by [`tests/unit/test_oscal_idle_trace_remarks.py`](../tests/unit/test_oscal_idle_trace_remarks.py), empirically verified `9 failed` red on `0ec2a7f7^` and `10 passed` green on `0ec2a7f7`.

### POAM-2026-216: Synthetic Producer-Stub Fixture (`DEFAULT_JOB_LOGS`) and Negative-Grep Gate W Log Check Passing Vacuously Without Matching the Real `run_lula_audit.sh` Emitter

**Control:** NIST SA-11 (Developer Testing and Evaluation), CA-2 (Control Assessments), CA-7 (Continuous Monitoring)
**Risk Level:** Moderate
**Status:** Closed (2026-11-14) — merged in `#748` (`0ec2a7f7`)
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-14
**Target Closure:** 2026-11-30

**Description:**
1. **Vacuous synthetic fixture inside a vacuity-rejection test:** In [`tests/infrastructure/test_staging_lifecycle.py`](../tests/infrastructure/test_staging_lifecycle.py), `DEFAULT_JOB_LOGS` supplied a five-line hand-written string (`assessment-results:\n  observations:\n ... POST /v1/infra/events -> ...`) to `Job/lula-gate-w` in Gate W Phase 3 tests that bore no structural relation to [`infra/modules/lula_cron/run_lula_audit.sh`](../infra/modules/lula_cron/run_lula_audit.sh)'s real stdout, yet passed Phase 3 because [`scripts/staging_lifecycle.sh`](../scripts/staging_lifecycle.sh) relied on negative regexes (`not-satisfied`, `lula-validation-error`, `startup_grace`) finding nothing in it.

**Remediation & Closure Verification (2026-11-14):**
1. `#748` (`0ec2a7f7`) enforced closed-world `lula.assessment_remark` status tokens on `a52`/`a53`/`a92` and emitted canonical `cage_lula_audit_receipt_v1` JSON lines in [`infra/modules/lula_cron/run_lula_audit.sh`](../infra/modules/lula_cron/run_lula_audit.sh), and updated [`verify_lula_gate_w_job_logs()`](../scripts/verify_lula_assessment_results.py) (`--lula-manifests-dir compliance/lula` in [`scripts/staging_lifecycle.sh`](../scripts/staging_lifecycle.sh)) to enforce `startup_grace_count == 0` and exact bijective stem-set equality (`set(satisfied_controls) == set(active_stems)`) across all 26 active manifests via [`discover_active_lula_manifests()`](../scripts/verify_lula_assessment_results.py).
2. **Producer-to-consumer regression verification:** Guarded by [`tests/unit/test_oscal_idle_trace_remarks.py`](../tests/unit/test_oscal_idle_trace_remarks.py) (live `run_lula_audit.sh` stdout piped into `verify_lula_gate_w_job_logs()`) and [`tests/infrastructure/test_staging_lifecycle.py`](../tests/infrastructure/test_staging_lifecycle.py).

### POAM-2026-217: Silent Evidence-Loss and Outage-Inversion Paths on Stopped or Broken `EvidenceStreamSink` (`GOVERNANCE_SEAL_CONSUMED` and `_emit_proxy_pass_evidence`)

**Control:** NIST AU-5 (Response to Audit Logging Process Failures), AU-10 (Non-repudiation), AU-12 (Audit Record Generation), AC-3 (Access Enforcement), ISO/IEC 42001 A.5.2, A.9.2
**Risk Level:** High
**Status:** Open — remediated in code (`2026-11-14`), pending mainline squash-merge SHA
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-14
**Target Closure:** 2026-11-30

**Description:**
1. **Rank #1 — Single-use seal burned in DB 0 while skipping `GOVERNANCE_SEAL_CONSUMED` in DB 1 (`POAM-2026-156` audit half):** In [`src/gateway/governance/routing_seal.py`](../src/gateway/governance/routing_seal.py), `verify_and_consume_seal()` burned the single-use nonce in Redis DB 0 via `_atomic_burn_nonce()` and then wrapped both `sink.ingest(consumed_event)` and `if es.is_evidence_chain_blocking(): raise SymbolicGovernorViolation(...)` inside `if has_redis or getattr(sink, "is_running", False):`. On a stopped `EvidenceStreamSink` (`_redis is None`, `is_running is False` — e.g. during shutdown drain after `evidence_sink.stop()` in [`src/gateway/server/hybrid_server.py`](../src/gateway/server/hybrid_server.py)), the outer `if` evaluated to `False`, burning the single-use seal with zero `GOVERNANCE_SEAL_CONSUMED` audit record and returning `True` so the downstream tool executed un-evidenced.
2. **Rank #2 — Outage inversion on `POST /v1/chat/completions` (`A.5.2` & `A.9.2`):** In [`src/gateway/server/inference_proxy.py`](../src/gateway/server/inference_proxy.py), `_emit_proxy_evidence()` failed closed with HTTP `503` on refusals via `commit_decision_evidence()`, whereas `_emit_proxy_pass_evidence()` ignored `is_evidence_chain_blocking()`, returned `None` silently when `not sink._running`, ignored `None` returns from `sink.ingest()`, and swallowed `EvidenceChainUnavailableError` / `EvidenceChainCorruptError` as `WARNING` logs. During a Redis custody outage, CAGE refused to emit un-evidenced denials (`503`) while serving permitted completions and Stage 4 PII-redacted responses (`200 OK`) with zero `INFERENCE_PROXY_STAGE1_PASS` (`A.5.2`) or `INFERENCE_PROXY_PII_SCRUB_PASS` (`A.9.2`) records.
3. **Rank #3 — Undocumented dual sink source of truth:** Only `inference_proxy.py` read `getattr(request.app.state, "evidence_sink", None)` ahead of [`get_evidence_sink()`](../src/gateway/governance/evidence/stream.py), allowing a stopped sink left on `app.state` to shadow the module-level singleton.
4. **Rank #4 — Undetected evidence loss across telemetry & compliance planes:** `cage_gateway_gated_requests_total{outcome="permitted"}` incremented in `WorkloadIdentityMiddleware` independently of Redis appends, while `compliance-bridge` computed `total_traces` solely from custody records — making an evidence-dropping gateway look idle rather than broken.

**Remediation Plan:**
1. Route `GOVERNANCE_SEAL_CONSUMED` in [`verify_and_consume_seal()`](../src/gateway/governance/routing_seal.py) unconditionally through [`commit_decision_evidence()`](../src/gateway/governance/evidence/stream.py) when `is_evidence_chain_blocking()` is `True`, raising `SymbolicGovernorViolation` and incrementing `cage_governance_evidence_publish_failures_total{kind="seal_consumed"}` on any stopped or failing sink.
2. Route `INFERENCE_PROXY_STAGE1_PASS` (`A.5.2`) and `INFERENCE_PROXY_PII_SCRUB_PASS` (`A.9.2`) in [`_emit_proxy_pass_evidence()`](../src/gateway/server/inference_proxy.py) through `commit_decision_evidence()` under `is_evidence_chain_blocking()`, rolling back reserved token quota and returning HTTP `503` (`evidence_chain_unavailable`) across both streaming and non-streaming completions before releasing any completion bytes.
3. Retire `app.state.evidence_sink` and `inference_app.state.evidence_sink` across [`hybrid_server.py`](../src/gateway/server/hybrid_server.py) and [`inference_proxy.py`](../src/gateway/server/inference_proxy.py) so `get_evidence_sink()` is the sole source of truth across Layer 1.
4. Expose `cage_gateway_evidence_records_appended_total` (incremented only inside [`EvidenceStreamSink._acknowledge()`](../src/gateway/governance/evidence/stream.py) and `append_evidence_record_sync()` after Redis `XADD` acknowledgement) and `cage_gateway_evidenced_requests_permitted_total` ([`WorkloadIdentityMiddleware`](../src/gateway/server/workload_identity.py)), guarded by `absent_over_time` and reconciled in [`google_monitoring_alert_policy.gateway_evidence_append_reconciliation`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/metrics_alerting.tf) (`AU-5 / AU-12`), with red-before-green tests in [`tests/unit/test_fail_closed_evidence_paths.py`](../tests/unit/test_fail_closed_evidence_paths.py).

**Closure Criteria:**
1. `verify_and_consume_seal()` and `_emit_proxy_pass_evidence()` fail closed on stopped/broken/corrupt sinks under `EVIDENCE_CHAIN_BLOCKING=true`, `app.state.evidence_sink` / `inference_app.state.evidence_sink` are absent from Layer 1, `gateway_evidence_append_reconciliation` is tested in [`lula_cron.tftest.hcl`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/tests/lula_cron.tftest.hcl), and red-before-green tests in [`tests/unit/test_fail_closed_evidence_paths.py`](../tests/unit/test_fail_closed_evidence_paths.py) binding `POAM-2026-217` pass on `main` with recorded squash-merge SHA.

**Note (`2026-11-16`, `POAM-2026-230`; closed `2026-11-23`):** Closure criterion 1's tftest originally proved only that `gateway_evidence_append_reconciliation` was planned while `notification_channels` defaulted to `[]`. With `POAM-2026-230` closed (`#859` `fc0152a8`, `#862` `5fa41805`), [`lula_cron.tftest.hcl`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/tests/lula_cron.tftest.hcl) enforces plan-time channel validity across all 9 policies and `gateway_evidence_append_reconciliation` routes to CAGE's verified Pub/Sub terminal sink (`topics/cage-staging-alerts` → `subscriptions/cage-staging-alerts-verify`; downstream human paging fan-out is adopter-operated). Ranks #1 to #3 fail closed in code and do not depend on the alarm.

### POAM-2026-218: Retire Opt-In provider_01 v0.2 Compatibility Path at FlowSignal v0.3 Sandbox Cutover (EU_ECB)

**Control:** NIST CM-7 (Least Functionality), SA-8 (Security and Privacy Engineering Principles), AC-3 (Access Enforcement)
**Risk Level:** Moderate
**Status:** Open — bound to `POAM-2026-113` and `POAM-2026-156` (item 2) FlowSignal Phase 3 `v0.3` sandbox cutover
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-14
**Target Closure:** 2026-12-31

**Description:**
To prepare CAGE's side of the bilateral Phase 3 `v0.3` revision ([`FLOWSIGNAL_PHASE3_V03_ADDENDUM.md`](partners/provider_01/FLOWSIGNAL_PHASE3_V03_ADDENDUM.md)) without breaking live over-the-wire CI runs (`ci-partner-integration.yml`) against FlowSignal's currently deployed Phase 3 `v0.2` Cloud Run service, [`Provider01NormativeProvider`](../src/integrations/provider_01/provider.py) introduces `PROVIDER_01_CONTRACT_VERSION` (`"v0.2"` default vs. opt-in `"v0.3"` strict mode). While `"v0.2"` remains in [`provider.py`](../src/integrations/provider_01/provider.py), default deployments that omit `PROVIDER_01_CONTRACT_VERSION=v0.3` still execute the legacy `v0.2` request builder (permissive `params.get(..., default)` fallbacks and optional receipt expiry). Per `AGENTS.md` (clean architecture over transitional dual-path retention), this dual-contract branch exists solely for the external partner staging cutover window and must never outlive `POAM-2026-113`.

**Remediation Plan:**
1. Deliver [`FLOWSIGNAL_PHASE3_V03_ADDENDUM.md`](partners/provider_01/FLOWSIGNAL_PHASE3_V03_ADDENDUM.md) to FlowSignal and coordinate staging Cloud Run promotion of Phase 3 `v0.3` (`authority_receipt.valid_until` RFC 3339 UTC expiry on `ALLOW` and strict verified-fact validation).
2. Enforce a self-checking CI guard (`test_poam_218_forbids_closing_poam_113_while_v02_dual_path_exists` in [`test_provider_01_v03_readiness.py`](../tests/integrations/provider_01/test_provider_01_v03_readiness.py)) that parses [`docs/POAM.md`](POAM.md) and [`src/integrations/provider_01/provider.py`](../src/integrations/provider_01/provider.py) on every PR and fails closed if `POAM-2026-113` or `POAM-2026-218` is moved to Closed or marked `Status: Closed` while `"v0.2"` or `PROVIDER_01_CONTRACT_VERSION` remains in [`provider.py`](../src/integrations/provider_01/provider.py).
3. At partner sandbox cutover, delete `"v0.2"` and `PROVIDER_01_CONTRACT_VERSION` so strict `v0.3` is the sole code path.

**Closure Criteria:**
1. When FlowSignal deploys Phase 3 `v0.3` on its staging Cloud Run sandbox, the cutover PR simultaneously (a) deletes `"v0.2"`, `PROVIDER_01_CONTRACT_VERSION`, all permissive `params.get(..., default)` fallbacks in [`_build_cage_authority_request()`](../src/integrations/provider_01/provider.py), and optional-receipt-validity fallback in [`provider.py`](../src/integrations/provider_01/provider.py), making strict `v0.3` the sole code path, and (b) closes `POAM-2026-113`, `POAM-2026-156` (item 2), and `POAM-2026-218` together on a live over-the-wire sandbox pass (`ci-partner-integration.yml`).

### POAM-2026-219: Lula Manifests Rated or Cited Beyond What Their Rego Checks

**Control:** NIST CA-2 (Control Assessments), CA-7 (Continuous Monitoring), SA-11 (Developer Testing and Evaluation)
**Risk Level:** Moderate
**Status:** Open — the `#664` instances remediated 2026-11-14, pending the mainline squash-merge SHA and a Gate W run of the restored `iso001-token-quota` check; the earlier citations listed below await a later fix
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-14
**Target Closure:** 2026-11-30

**Description:**
[`compliance/lula/README.md`](../compliance/lula/README.md) rates every Lula manifest, and only a manifest it rates Active may back a POA&M closure ([`check_poam_lula_divergence.py`](../scripts/check_poam_lula_divergence.py)). Checked against their Rego on 2026-11-14, six Active rows described checks the Rego does not make, and so did the manifests' own headers and `Notes:`.

**Mechanism:** `#664` (`372daad2`, 2026-11-06) migrated all 33 manifests to the Lula v0.16 `resource-rule` / `requests` schema. In the same diff it removed assertions from these six without changing their README rows, headers, `Notes:` or the POA&M entries that cited them, and its commit message describes a schema migration and mentions no removals. A thirty-three-file schema migration is a diff in which nobody compares what each manifest asserts before and after. `#664` is also the change in which `F-109`'s hollow RA-5 `NetworkPolicy` check was amended out before push, so hollow checks were on reviewers' minds in that change, and the six removals still went through. The Rego of all six was unchanged from `372daad2` until this remediation; the later edits to these files (`#686`, `#705`) did not touch it.

| Manifest | What `#664` removed | What the Rego asserts now | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ftra` | Rules named for FTRA configuration, the terminal registry ConfigMap and an interim NetworkPolicy. Each passed whenever the gateway container existed, and the gateway rule matched only a Deployment named `cage-gateway`, which Terraform does not create | `gateway_exists`: a gateway Deployment with a `gateway` container | Rated Stub. Withdrawn from POAM-2026-030-B and POAM-2026-074, which stand on `tests/test_ftra_package.py` |
| `eu-fria` | `CAGE_NORMATIVE_PROVIDER` set and not `static`; `CAGE_NORMATIVE_ENDPOINT` set; region `EU_ECB` | `gateway_running` and `region_from_configmap`, which accepts any of the three regions; satisfied under `US_FED` in certified Gate W | Rated Stub. Withdrawn from POAM-2026-099, whose closure stands on `tests/governor/test_jurisdiction_wiring.py` (correction in that section) |
| `tqp007` | `TOKEN_QUOTA_FAIL_CLOSED=true` on a `token-quota-proxy` Deployment; neither the variable nor the Deployment appears in the committed Terraform or source | `tqp_running` and `tqp_has_redis_url` | Rated Stub |
| `flowsignal` | `CAGE_NORMATIVE_PROVIDER=provider_01` | Four rules; its Redis namespace check compares constants in the Rego | Rated Stub |
| `iso001-token-quota` | The advisor readiness check, and the check that a policy file contains `quota_available` and `token_quota`, which became a non-empty ConfigMap check; its `REDIS_URL` check was widened to the gateway or the advisor | `gateway_has_redis_url` and the restored `opa_policy_has_quota_rules` | Stays Active with the policy-content check restored. The advisor readiness check is not restored; no manifest checks the advisor's readiness, and `sc4`, `ac3` and `au12` check the gateway's |
| `sc8` | Checks 1–4: TLS Service ports, `default-deny-ingress`, Ingress TLS, and `readOnlyRootFilesystem` or a TLS annotation on every Deployment | `redis_ca_pinned`: Memorystore CA pinning | Stays Active with its header and `Notes:` corrected, including a false "Remediates POAM-011" (POAM-011 is open). Withdrawn from POAM-2026-080, -167 and -195; still cited by POAM-2026-086, whose subject it is |

Three of the removals checked configuration the committed Terraform did not set at `372daad2`: the gateway carried neither `CAGE_NORMATIVE_PROVIDER` nor `CAGE_NORMATIVE_ENDPOINT`, `staging.tfvars` set `US_FED`, and `TOKEN_QUOTA_FAIL_CLOSED` appears nowhere. `eu-fria`, `flowsignal` and `tqp007` would each have failed once Lula ran against the cluster. The evidence-claim census found the same thing: graded against the files as they stood before `#664` (it merged in `#679` the next day), it records that `eu-fria`, `flowsignal` and `ftra` could not pass on a Terraform-built cluster, because each selected a `cage-gateway` Deployment Terraform does not create and `eu-fria` and `flowsignal` asserted provider settings nothing sets. `#664` widened the Deployment match and deleted the unmet assertions instead of meeting them, so the manifests went from unable to pass to passing without checking what they claimed. Whether `sc8`'s and `iso001-token-quota`'s removed checks would have passed was not established. `ftra` asserted no more before `#664` than after it.

POAM-2026-099 is the case that mattered: it cited `eu-fria` as `satisfied` in certified Gate W for `FriaTier` wiring while the manifest checked neither the tier nor the region. No closure falls, because each affected closure also cites tests that bind it; POAM-2026-099's tests were re-verified by breaking each closed element (correction in that section).

**Earlier citations of manifests already rated Stub (found 2026-11-14; fixed in a later change).** The overstatement is older than `#664` wherever a closure or a statement cites as evidence a manifest the README already rated Stub. Every closed row and detail section in the five POA&M ledgers, with struck text ignored, and every row of the evidence-claim census were scanned for citations of manifests not rated Active:

| Where | Cites | What it should rest on |
|---|---|---|
| Closed POAM-2026-079, row and detail section | `lula-validation-ac2.yaml`, rated Stub | [`test_workload_identity_partition.py`](../tests/infrastructure/test_workload_identity_partition.py) and [`test_trade_governance_e2e.py`](../tests/test_trade_governance_e2e.py), which it also cites. The citation is to be struck once the closure is re-verified on those tests, as POAM-2026-099's was |
| US SSP `g7000001` (AC-2, `partially-implemented`) | `lula-validation-ac2.yaml`, whose three `validate` rules are alternatives, so any one passing satisfies it | Already graded `WEAKER` with disposition `restate` in the census; the restatement is pending |
| US SSP `g7000020` (AARM vectors) and `g7000021` to `g7000025` (AI 600-1 CBRN, confabulation, data privacy, human-AI configuration and prompt injection), formerly `implemented` | `lula-validation-aarm-vectors.yaml` and the five `ai600` manifests, each as the statement's validation; all six are rated Stub, and the five `ai600` manifests' own metadata says they always pass | **Folded into `POAM-2026-235` (`2026-11-17`):** all six SSP statements moved to `partially-implemented` and restated onto their code/unit tests with explicit `Stub` disclaimers, and their census grades moved from vacuous `HOLDS` on [`test_lula_v0160_schema.py`](../tests/test_lula_v0160_schema.py) to `WEAKER` |

The scan also matched two entries that name a non-Active manifest without resting on it: POAM-2026-102's detail section names `cm6` and `mas-trm-s6` to say why Lula was not run, and US SSP `h8000005-0000-4000-8000-000000000006` says `cm6` cannot pass. Neither is an instance. [`check_poam_lula_divergence.py`](../scripts/check_poam_lula_divergence.py) records a citation of a non-Active manifest in a closed entry as a diagnostic and passes the entry when another citation binds it, which is how POAM-2026-079's citation stood.

**Remediation (2026-11-14):**
1. `ftra`, `eu-fria`, `tqp007` and `flowsignal` rated Stub. Their headers and `Notes:` state what each asserts and what `#664` removed.
2. `iso001-token-quota`'s `opa_policy_has_quota_rules` restored. Lula v0.16.0 (`lula dev validate`) evaluated it against synthetic resources built from the bundle Terraform deploys (`local.domain_opa_policies` in [`infra/targets/gcp-gke/main.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/main.tf)): satisfied with the finance bundle (`trade_governance.rego`), not satisfied with the healthcare bundle, and not satisfied with a non-empty bundle that carries no quota rule, which is the case `#664`'s check passed. No Gate W run has evaluated it yet.
3. `sc8`'s header and `Notes:` describe its one check.
4. Lula citations withdrawn, struck through with a dated note, from POAM-2026-030-B, -074, -080, -099, -167 and -195, and from `EU-001` in [`POAM_EU_ECB.md`](compliance/eu_ecb/POAM_EU_ECB.md).
5. Every Active row in [`compliance/lula/README.md`](../compliance/lula/README.md) names the rules its `validate` composes. [`tests/unit/test_lula_description_parity.py`](../tests/unit/test_lula_description_parity.py) fails when a row names a rule the Rego does not define or omits one `validate` composes, and checks that it covers exactly the closure allowlist. Replaying `#664` against it, with rows naming the rules each `validate` composed before `#664`, reports a missing rule for all six, including `eu-fria`'s `region_is_eu_ecb` and the `ftra` rules named for retired resources. It compares names, not bodies, so it cannot see what a rule selects; item 7 holds that.
6. The OSCAL statements and evidence-claim census entries that relied on the four re-rated manifests are restated.
7. [`check_k8s_terraform_parity.py`](../scripts/check_k8s_terraform_parity.py), which already failed a NetworkPolicy, Service or PodMonitoring selector that matches no Terraform workload, now also fails an Active Lula manifest that selects, by name, an object no Terraform resource, `locals` manifest or Helm template in `infra/` creates, unless it is a declared platform object whose enabling setting Terraform sets: the `anetd` DaemonSet, allowed while the GKE module resolves `datapath_provider` to `ADVANCED_DATAPATH`. Every alternate in a set must exist, and a `metadata.name` test it cannot read fails closed. [`tests/unit/test_lula_selector_parity.py`](../tests/unit/test_lula_selector_parity.py) plants each case and replays `#664`: every object `ftra` selected by name before it (a `cage-gateway` Deployment, a terminal-registry ConfigMap and two NetworkPolicies) is one `infra/` does not create, and so are the `cage-gateway` Deployment `eu-fria` and `flowsignal` selected, `tqp007`'s `token-quota-proxy` Deployment and `iso001-token-quota`'s `opa-policy` ConfigMap. The check rejected two dead alternates in Active manifests, `stera-gateway` in `au12` and `opa-policy` in `iso001-token-quota`; both were removed, and neither could have matched an object on a cluster Terraform builds. Eleven of the fourteen evaluated stubs still select a name `infra/` does not create, ten of them `stera-gateway`, which `#664` wrote into eleven manifests; promoting any of them runs the check. Neither this check nor item 5 judges whether a rule checks enough of what it selects: today's `ftra` would pass both without its dead alternates, which is why it is rated Stub.

**Closure Criteria:**
1. Merged to `main`, with the squash-merge SHA recorded here, and [`tests/unit/test_lula_description_parity.py`](../tests/unit/test_lula_description_parity.py) and [`tests/unit/test_lula_selector_parity.py`](../tests/unit/test_lula_selector_parity.py), both binding `POAM-2026-219`, passing on `main`.
2. A Gate W run on a tree containing the restored check records `lula-validation-iso001-token-quota.yaml` `satisfied` and a `lula.rating_breakdown` of 12 rated Active. The in-region `APAC_MAS` run planned for the residency change can serve, because the check is evaluated in every region. A merge SHA alone does not close this entry: the finding is that checks were recorded as satisfied without evidence they could be satisfied.
3. Each earlier citation listed above is corrected: POAM-2026-079's citation of `ac2` struck with a dated note once its closure is re-verified on the tests it also cites, US SSP `g7000001` restated, and the six `Stub`-backed US SSP statements (`g7000020`..`g7000025`) merged via `POAM-2026-235`.

### POAM-2026-220: Latent Production `compliance-bridge` Startup Failure in `resolve_cold_store_bucket()` Masked by `staging` Residency Bypass

**Control:** NIST SC-7 (Boundary Protection), AU-9 (Protection of Audit Information), CA-7 (Continuous Monitoring), GDPR Art. 44, MAS TRM §4.2
**Status:** Open — remediated in code (`2026-11-15`); held Open pending mainline squash-merge SHA and a Gate W run with residency active in `staging`
**Severity:** High

**Description:**
1. **`staging` bypassed geographic residency, hiding a broken `prod` path.** [`resolve_cold_store_bucket()`](../src/gateway/governance/evidence/residency.py) skipped geographic validation whenever `CAGE_ENV` was in `("development", "dev", "test", "ci", "staging", "uat", "preprod")`. Because Gate W executes with `CAGE_ENV=staging`, no Gate W run ever exercised the runtime cold-store residency gate (`residency_result_breakdown` in [`compliance/gate_w_certification.json`](../compliance/gate_w_certification.json)).
2. **Verified production failure (`2026-11-15`).** Under the environment `module.compliance_bridge` rendered for `prod` (`CAGE_ENV=prod`, `CAGE_DEPLOYMENT_REGION=US_FED`, `EVIDENCE_COLD_STORE=gcs`, `EVIDENCE_COLD_STORE_BUCKET=<PROJECT_ID>-evidence-worm-prod`, and no `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`), `resolve_cold_store_bucket(backend_id="gcs")` raised `ResidencyViolationError` because `<PROJECT_ID>-evidence-worm-prod` did not match the legacy `allowed_prefixes` (`"us-"`, `"cage-us-"`) and no cloud location variable was present. [`EvidenceCustodian.from_env()`](../src/compliance_bridge/evidence_custodian.py) therefore failed during `compliance-bridge` lifespan startup in `prod`, while the identical inputs passed under `CAGE_ENV=staging`.
3. **Weak proxies and `bucket=` short-circuit.** Bucket-name prefixes (`allowed_prefixes`) assert nothing about where a bucket actually resides, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` / `AWS_REGION` name the caller pod's region rather than the bucket's immutable location, and [`get_cold_store()`](../src/gateway/governance/evidence/factory.py) wrote `bucket or resolve_cold_store_bucket(...)`, skipping residency checks whenever a caller passed `bucket=` explicitly.
4. **Why `module.worm_bucket.bucket_location` over runtime `storage.buckets.get`.** In [`infra/targets/gcp-gke/iam.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/iam.tf) and [`infra/modules/evidence_domain/main.tf`](../infra/modules/evidence_domain/main.tf), `compliance-bridge` holds append-only `roles/storage.objectCreator` (plus `roles/storage.objectViewer` when in-project), neither of which grants `storage.buckets.get`. Querying bucket metadata at runtime would require granting `roles/storage.legacyBucketReader` on the WORM bucket (widening read/list permissions on the custodian identity) and importing cloud SDKs into Layer 1 (`FORBIDDEN_VENDOR_SDKS`). Instead, [`infra/modules/worm_bucket/outputs.tf`](../infra/modules/worm_bucket/outputs.tf) outputs `bucket_location` directly from the managed `google_storage_bucket.bucket[0].location` or external `data.google_storage_bucket.external[0].location` (an immutable GCS bucket property), and [`infra/modules/compliance_bridge/main.tf`](../infra/modules/compliance_bridge/main.tf) injects it as `EVIDENCE_COLD_STORE_LOCATION` with a plan-time `lifecycle.precondition`.

**Remediation (`2026-11-15`):**
1. [`resolve_cold_store_bucket()`](../src/gateway/governance/evidence/residency.py) enforces geographic residency across all `is_enforcing()` postures (`production`, `staging`, `local`, or an unknown `CAGE_ENV`), skipping only in `dev`, `test` and `ci`.
2. [`config/compliance/residency.json`](../config/compliance/residency.json) and `RegionalResidencyRule` drop `allowed_prefixes`, `allow_prefixes`, `default_bucket`, and `LOCAL`, and `resolve_cold_store_bucket()` drops `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` / `AWS_REGION` fallbacks, requiring `location` or `EVIDENCE_COLD_STORE_LOCATION` (case-insensitively matched against `allowed_locations`).
3. [`get_cold_store()`](../src/gateway/governance/evidence/factory.py) passes `bucket_override=bucket` to `resolve_cold_store_bucket()`.
4. [`infra/modules/worm_bucket/outputs.tf`](../infra/modules/worm_bucket/outputs.tf), [`infra/modules/compliance_bridge/main.tf`](../infra/modules/compliance_bridge/main.tf), and [`infra/targets/gcp-gke/main.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/main.tf) wire `module.worm_bucket.bucket_location` into `EVIDENCE_COLD_STORE_LOCATION` with a plan-time `lifecycle.precondition` on `kubernetes_deployment.compliance_bridge`, and [`scripts/read_worm_chain_anchor.py`](../scripts/read_worm_chain_anchor.py) resolves `EVIDENCE_COLD_STORE_LOCATION` from `gcloud storage buckets describe` for pre-provision host anchor checks.
5. Guarded by [`tests/test_evidence_residency.py`](../tests/test_evidence_residency.py) (binding `POAM-2026-220`), [`infra/modules/compliance_bridge/tests/operator_identity.tftest.hcl`](../infra/modules/compliance_bridge/tests/operator_identity.tftest.hcl), and [`tests/infrastructure/test_evidence_custody_wiring.py`](../tests/infrastructure/test_evidence_custody_wiring.py).

**Closure Criteria:**
1. Merged to `main` with the squash-merge SHA recorded here, and [`tests/test_evidence_residency.py`](../tests/test_evidence_residency.py) and [`operator_identity.tftest.hcl`](../infra/modules/compliance_bridge/tests/operator_identity.tftest.hcl) passing on `main`.
2. A Gate W run on a tree containing this lock brings `compliance-bridge` ready with `EVIDENCE_COLD_STORE_LOCATION` enforced in `staging` and verifies custodied WORM evidence chains (`verified >= 1`, `gaps == 0`).
