### POAM-2026-222: Threshold Traceability Matrix Monitoring Column Cites Telemetry That Was Never Emitted

**Control:** NIST CA-7 (Continuous Monitoring), RA-3 (Risk Assessment), SI-4 (System Monitoring), PM-9 (Risk Management Strategy)
**Risk Level:** Moderate, conditional on the signing hold below; High if any of RA-001–RA-004 is signed before every row has a disposition
**Status:** Open
**Owner:** Authorizing Official, the signatory of RA-001–RA-004 in CAGE-TTM-001 §5 and §6. Re-pointing and implementation can be delegated; withdrawing a monitoring claim reopens the underlying risk, and only this role can re-accept it.
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-15
**Target Closure:** 2026-12-31

**Description:**
[`THRESHOLD_TRACEABILITY_MATRIX.md`](../compliance/risk_acceptance/THRESHOLD_TRACEABILITY_MATRIX.md) (CAGE-TTM-001) exists to show which telemetry watches which accepted risk. Its `Langfuse Metric` column names 26 `cage.*` metrics across 23 thresholds, and a repository-wide sweep on `2026-11-15` found that none has ever been emitted by `src/` or `infra/`. The column describes a backend that was never built: Langfuse holds no custom counters, gauges, or histograms in CAGE's design, and every metric CAGE emits is a `cage_*` Prometheus series. Appendix B states that the `cage.stpa.*`, `cage.security.*`, and `cage.consensus.*` families and `cage.model.confidence_below_threshold` are "emitted at 100% regardless of OTel sampling rate"; none exists.

**Vintage:** The matrix is dated `2026-03-06` and is present in full, column included, in root commit `1902c92c` (`2026-06-01`, the squash of pre-release history), so git cannot attribute it further back. The first metric emitter in `src/` landed in `afd4c2d1` (`2026-08-15`) and the first `cage_gateway_*` series in `f0ca9f4d` (`2026-11-14`). Thirteen later commits edited the file and none reconciled the column: it was written as a design specification and later read as a description of what exists. Seven other documents carry the same `2026-03-06` date and entered git in the same root commit; their detection sweep is recorded separately and is not a closure condition of this item.

**Blast radius (`2026-11-15`):** Zero OSCAL statements and zero of the 209 census rows cite the matrix or any of the 26 names. [`RISK_ASSESSMENT_REPORT.md`](../compliance/rar/RISK_ASSESSMENT_REPORT.md) does not cite it. `docs/partners/provider_05/veip_three_axioms_architecture.md` cites RA-001–RA-004 as a current-state gap (unsigned), not as reliance. RA-001–RA-004 all read `Authorizing Official (AO) — [SIGNATURE PENDING]`, so no executed acceptance rests on the column. That is an accident of timing, which the signing hold below turns into a control.

**Compensating controls withdrawn with the column:**
1. **RA-001 (1)** names a Langfuse compliance-project log as the 100% record of governance decisions and rests on Appendix B. Governance-decision custody is the Redis DB 1 `cage:evidence:stream` hot custody buffer feeding KMS-signed WORM archival (`POAM-2026-084`). Re-point to that custody evidence or withdraw.
2. **RA-002 (1)** states that `CronJob/lula-audit` injects a synthetic health-check governance evaluation. [`run_lula_audit.sh`](../infra/modules/lula_cron/run_lula_audit.sh) injects none: idle windows report `assessment_status=insufficient_traffic` (`POAM-2026-215`), and synthetic liveness probing is [`canary.py`](../src/gateway/canary.py).

**Signing hold (control condition):** RA-001, RA-002, RA-003, and RA-004 (CAGE-TTM-001 §5) and the CAGE-TTM-001 §6 approval block must not be signed until every §2.1 row carries an owner-recorded disposition below and its remediation is merged (A, B) or opened as its own POAM item (C). A signature applied before then rests on monitoring that does not exist and raises this item to High. The hold is stated at the top of the matrix and on its signature page.

**Proposed dispositions (owner to confirm per row):**

| Row(s) | Bucket | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| THR-FIN-002, THR-FIN-003, THR-FIN-004, THR-FIN-005 | **A — implement** | Add `cage_stpa_refusals_total{rule}`, a stage-level counter labelled by the STPA rule identifier the domain plugin reports. Not a sixth `tier` value: `trade_confidence`, `bounding`, `consensus`, `cbf`, and `fiscal` are domain tiers, STPA is a pipeline stage, and a single `tier="stpa"` could not separate FIN-1 from UCA-5 from UCA-6. Rule identifiers arrive from the plugin at runtime, so the kernel holds no domain literal (Gate G3) and the label set is bounded by the compiled rule set. STPA refusals emit no metric today. |
| THR-FIN-006 | **A** | Count consensus triggers above `consensus.threshold_usd`, not only dissent refusals. |
| THR-SEC-001 | **A** | Distinguish tier-1 keyword refusals (reason label or dedicated counter); `cage_gateway_gated_requests_total{outcome="blocked"}` carries no reason. |
| THR-LAT-001 | **A** | Count UCA-2 refusals through `cage_stpa_refusals_total{rule}` and export the measured quote age as a histogram. The risk is already controlled: [`trade_inputs.py`](../src/cage_finance/tools/trade_inputs.py) measures quote age at receipt on the server from the verified quote's publication time, and the UCA-2 rule in [`uca_rules.py`](../src/cage_finance/stpa/uca_rules.py) refuses a trade above the regional `max_latency_ms` and fails closed when the value is missing or non-numeric. Only visibility is missing: no metric counts UCA-2 refusals and the measured quote age is not exported. **Row correction:** the matrix names the row "Max Trade Round-Trip Latency", a quantity CAGE does not measure; it is renamed to quote age at receipt. |
| THR-FIN-001 | **B — re-point** | `cage_governance_refusals_total{tier="cbf"}`. |
| THR-CONF-001 | **B** | `cage_governance_refusals_total{tier="trade_confidence"}` and span `cage.confidence_check`. |
| THR-CON-001 | **B** (partial) | `cage_governance_refusals_total{tier="consensus"}` covers dissent refusals; the quorum-met rate is unobserved until THR-FIN-006's counter lands. |
| THR-AUD-002 | **B** | `cage_lula_audit_last_pass_timestamp_seconds` and `cage_lula_audit_deadman_breaches_total`. |
| THR-OBS-003, THR-OBS-004, THR-OBS-005 | **B** | Active Lula `a52`, `a53`, and `a92` and `cage_lula_audit_not_satisfied_controls`. |
| THR-CBF-001, THR-SAF-001 | **B** | Constants, not signals: startup schema validation of `config/governance_thresholds.json` and `config/safety_params.json` by `src/gateway/governance/schemas/thresholds.py`. |
| THR-AUD-001 | **B** | The retention configuration and [`retention_posture.tftest.hcl`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/tests/retention_posture.tftest.hcl); the matrix's 90-day figure must be reconciled with the tested values at disposition. |
| THR-OBS-001 | **B** | The configured OTel sampler. No check reads it today, so this row becomes A unless a check is named at disposition. |
| THR-OBS-002 | **B — sequenced** | Not before the zero-traffic reset is fixed: the compliance-bridge `evidence_age_seconds` resets to `0` on zero traffic, so re-pointing a 48-hour freshness threshold at it would replace a fictional metric with a false-green one. |
| THR-LAT-002, THR-LAT-003, THR-LAT-004 | **C — withdraw** | Informational SLA targets; nothing depends on them. |

**Note (`2026-11-16`, `POAM-2026-230`; closed `2026-11-23`):** Prior to `POAM-2026-230` (`#859` `fc0152a8`, `#862` `5fa41805`), THR-AUD-002's re-point fed only `lula_audit_failure` with no notification channel; `lula_audit_failure` now delivers to CAGE's verified Pub/Sub terminal sink (`topics/cage-staging-alerts` → `subscriptions/cage-staging-alerts-verify`), while no Cloud Monitoring policy reads the statistical `cage_lula_audit_last_pass_timestamp_seconds` gauge (auditor liveness is monitored via `cage_lula_audit_last_healthy_run_timestamp_seconds` / `cage_lula_audit_deadman_breaches_total`, `#858` `ddbbdc81`), and downstream human paging fan-out remains adopter-operated.

**Remediation:**
1. ✅ **`2026-11-15`:** Dated notices on CAGE-TTM-001 withdraw the column, Appendix B, RA-001 (1), and RA-002 (1) as evidence, leave every row unchanged, and state the signing hold at the top of the document and on its signature page.
2. Record the owner's disposition for every row.
3. Implement the A rows after Batch 1 merges (`Wave 1B` owns `src/gateway/governance/**`), with tests that a planted STPA refusal increments `cage_stpa_refusals_total` for its rule and that a planted non-STPA refusal does not. THR-LAT-001 also exports the measured quote age as a histogram, tested with a planted stale quote that is refused, counted, and observed.
4. Re-point the B rows; THR-OBS-002 only after the compliance-bridge `evidence_age_seconds` zero-traffic reset is fixed.
5. Withdraw the C rows (THR-LAT-002, THR-LAT-003, THR-LAT-004).
6. Rename THR-LAT-001 and its threshold description to the enforced quantity, quote age at receipt. This corrects the row itself and is separate from its monitoring disposition.
7. Bring the matrix under the planned mechanism-reference gate, so a metric name that resolves to no emitter fails CI. The gate's matrix scope is bound to this item's Open status, never an unverified waiver.

**Closure Criteria:**
1. Every §2.1 row carries an owner-recorded disposition, and every A and B action is merged and every C action is withdrawn or opened as its own POAM item.
2. THR-LAT-001's row and threshold description name the enforced quantity, quote age at receipt.
3. The mechanism-reference gate passes on the matrix with zero waivers.
4. The approval-block history shows RA-001–RA-004 were not signed before criterion 1 held.

### POAM-2026-224: Gate G9 Waiver Hid Citations of Artifacts That Never Existed, and `DOC_SCOPE` Leaves Most of `docs/` Unverified

**Control:** NIST CA-2 (Control Assessments), CA-7 (Continuous Monitoring), PL-2 (System Security and Privacy Plans)
**Risk Level:** Moderate
**Status:** Open
**Owner:** Maintainer (Gate G9)
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-15
**Target Closure:** 2026-12-31

**Description:**
Gate G9 ([`check_doc_references.py`](../scripts/check_doc_references.py)) carried a `KNOWN_DOCUMENTED_GAPS` waiver of 162 entries naming 160 targets (two entries repeat a path with a `:<line>` suffix). Classified against git history on `2026-11-15`, 129 targets never existed in any commit, 28 were retired, and 3 exist at HEAD. The waiver's comment described its entries as deliberate NIST RMF gap citations, but the gate skipped them in every document in scope, in path resolution, file-path checks, and Python-symbol checks alike. It therefore hid the 2026-Q1 SAR and the authorization boundary document citing a security assessment plan at a path that exists in no commit (re-pointed there by `a2a338b8` after the draft plan they first cited was deleted in `00442dec`), and the SSP outline citing never-existent OSCAL assessment-plan and POA&M files. These citations were found by hand in the sweep of the `2026-03-06` document cohort, not by the gate.

**Scope without the waiver (measured at `eca0c553`):**

| Scope | Documents | Broken references | Documents affected |
|---|---|---|---|
| Current `DOC_SCOPE` | 69 | 17 | 9 |
| `DOC_SCOPE` plus `docs/compliance/**` | 101 | 237 | 24 |
| All of `docs/` except `docs/partners/**` | 179 | 299 | 52 |

The widest scope's 299 references name 166 distinct targets: 134 never existed and 32 were retired. Until this change, `AGENTS.md` named only `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/partners/**` as outside the scope, so every other document read as verified.

**Remediation:**
1. ✅ **`2026-11-15` (this change):** The waiver is deleted with its three uses. The 17 references are corrected, or pinned to a mainline commit where the path existed. The SAR is retracted to [`compliance/archive/retracted/SAR_2026Q1.md`](../compliance/archive/retracted/SAR_2026Q1.md) under a dated notice, because no in-place correction yields a true record of an assessment that did not happen. G9 verifies a retracted record's first-line notice and its POAM row before skipping the preserved body, and verifies the examples in branch-naming tables against their branch patterns instead of the filesystem. `AGENTS.md` states the real scope.
2. Widen `DOC_SCOPE` area by area (reference counts at `eca0c553`): `docs/compliance/us_fed` (177 references), `docs/compliance/cross-region` (21), `docs/compliance/REGION_GUARD_AUDIT.md` (13), the rest of `docs/compliance`, then the rest of `docs/`. Each change adds its area and corrects that area's references. A citation of a never-existent artifact as current evidence gets its own POAM item, not just rewording. A citation of an artifact that is deliberately missing uses a marker G9 verifies: the path must not exist and must name an open POAM item.
3. ✅ **`2026-11-15` (this change):** A regression test fails if `KNOWN_DOCUMENTED_GAPS` returns ([`test_check_doc_references.py`](../tests/test_check_doc_references.py)).
4. ✅ **`2026-11-20` (agent-context size gate discovery, truncation cutoff & CI wiring):** Replaced the single hard-coded [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) check and binary `24,576`-byte cap in [`check_agents_size.py`](../scripts/check_agents_size.py) with `discover_injected_agent_files()` and `classify_injected_rel_path()` (`DIRECTORY_RULE_FILENAMES` + `CUSTOMIZATION_DIRS` covering hierarchical directory rules, workspace rules such as [`.agents/rules/reasoning.md`](../.agents/rules/reasoning.md) and [`.agents/rules/security.md`](../.agents/rules/security.md), skills, custom agents, workflows such as [`.agents/workflows/enforce_cloud_build.md`](../.agents/workflows/enforce_cloud_build.md), and Copilot instruction files), set `MAX_BYTES = 24000` to match the observed ~`24,000`-byte truncation cutoff (closing the `24,001..24,576`-byte silent-cut band) with `MIN_INJECTED_FILES = 3` (catching discovery collapse without tripping on workflow churn), and wired `check_agents_size.py` into `ci.yml::lint`, [`setup_git_hooks.sh`](../scripts/setup_git_hooks.sh), and `Makefile::docs-check` ([`test_check_agents_size.py`](../tests/unit/test_check_agents_size.py)). **Boundary:** host-level instruction files under `~/.gemini/config/rules/` are also injected into agent context under the same ~`24,000`-byte truncation ceiling and sit outside any repository-scoped gate.

**Closure Criteria:**
1. `DOC_SCOPE` covers every Markdown document under the current roots plus all of `docs/` except `docs/partners/**`, and G9 validates `#heading-slug` anchors.
2. Retracted records carry verified notices.
3. G9 and [`check_agents_size.py`](../scripts/check_agents_size.py) pass on `main` with no waiver.

### POAM-2026-225: Telemetry Exported Raw Prompts and End-User IDs, and the PIA's 90-Day Purge Does Not Exist

**Control:** NIST AU-3(3) (Limit Personally Identifiable Information Elements), SI-12(3) (Information Disposal), RA-8 (Privacy Impact Assessments)
**Risk Level:** Low, resting on the attributed statement below; High for any deployment that processes real prompts on a build without remediation items 2 and 9
**Status:** Closed (2026-11-16) — remediated across `#772` (`4ab01bb4`), `#774` (`b12706d4`), `#775` (`1f274dd7`), `#778` (`fc7ac50a`), `#779` (`ae3e9b34`), `#780` (`775284e4`), `#781` (`87f4dca7`), `#782` (`8a3e86bb`), and `#783` (`5d98e1e2`), and verified live on `cage-staging`
**Owner:** Maintainer
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-15
**Target Closure:** 2026-12-31
**Date Closed:** 2026-11-16

**Description:**
[`PRIVACY_IMPACT_ASSESSMENT.md`](../compliance/pia/PRIVACY_IMPACT_ASSESSMENT.md) (draft v1.0, pending Privacy Officer review) stated in §6.1 that raw prompts were purged automatically after 90 days and only redacted summaries were kept for seven years, and in §6.2 that raw PII was never persisted in traces. No purge mechanism existed in `src/` or `infra/`, and raw content reached Langfuse (not audit custody) unredacted:
- [`server.py`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/server.py) set the raw user prompt on the advisor's request span (`gen_ai.input.messages` and the trace store's observation input) and the authenticated end-user ID (`enduser.id`).
- [`inference_proxy.py`](../src/gateway/server/inference_proxy.py) set the chat input and output messages on the gateway's inference span, sanitised only for multimodal content, and the gateway telemetry helper's `genai_span` set the prompt.
- Both workload modules ([`governed_advisor`](../infra/modules/governed_advisor/main.tf) and [`gateway`](../infra/modules/gateway/main.tf)) enabled httpx request and response body capture and GenAI message capture.

NeMo's PII scrubbing covers only NeMo's own spans, and NeMo has been off by default since `POAM-2026-125`. Langfuse (not audit custody) writes every raw ingestion event to its event bucket, which every non-staging tier locks for 2555 days ([`main.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/main.tf)), so that lock and the PIA's 90-day promise governed the same data. The decision was to keep the promise and change what reaches the bucket, not to amend the PIA to seven years, which would ratify the defect.

**Live state (staging project, read `2026-11-15`):**
- The event bucket retired under `POAM-2026-159` holds 35,639 objects written 2026-05-21 to 2026-10-29, including prompt text and end-user IDs, under a locked 2555-day retention policy. Retention runs from each object's creation, so the objects expire from 2033-05-19 to 2033-10-27. The bucket has no CMEK, so cryptographic erasure is unavailable, and nothing can purge it sooner.
- Three older event buckets (2026-02-21 to 2026-03-20, about 428,000 objects) and 78 persistent disks orphaned by deleted clusters (the trace store's ClickHouse, Postgres, MinIO, Redis and ZooKeeper operational-telemetry volumes — not audit custody — created 2026-01-26 to 2026-09-28) had no retention control at all.
- No production deployment exists in this project or in any other project visible to the maintainer.

**Basis for the severity and the disposal (attributed):** Maintainer, `2026-11-15`: "all data is synthetic data [used] for testing purposes." The Low rating and the disposal of the unlocked stores rest on that statement, and no artifact proves it. It is consistent with a field-presence scan of the locked bucket on `2026-11-15` that printed no content: all 5,522 request spans (May to October, plus March) came from private addresses; none carried `X-Forwarded-For` or a browser user agent; no span named a partner adapter; and the user IDs were synthetic-pattern strings, opaque identifiers, or a single script constant. Partner over-the-wire runs call partner endpoints from CAGE's adapters and do not pass through the advisor.

**Remediation:**
1. ✅ **`2026-11-15` (staging immediate containment, superseded by item 8):** the advisor's trace export was turned off and the advisor scaled to zero, and httpx body and GenAI content capture were turned off on the advisor and the gateway.
2. ✅ **`2026-11-15`, `#774` (`b12706d4`, `TC-1`):** prompt and response content and end-user identifiers are removed at every telemetry source (`#775` `1f274dd7` aligned OSCAL SSP and component-definition narratives). An exporter-side filter ([`content_filter.py`](../src/gateway/observability/content_filter.py)) drops content and identity keys, and drops rather than exports any span it cannot sanitise. Both modules set the capture variables to `"false"`, and [`test_telemetry_content_capture.py`](../tests/infrastructure/test_telemetry_content_capture.py) fails if either stops. Canary tests plant a prompt and a user ID and find neither in any exported span ([`test_telemetry_content_filter.py`](../tests/test_telemetry_content_filter.py)).
3. ✅ **`2026-11-15`:** the locked bucket's IAM is reduced to the project owner. An IAM deny policy (tag `privacy-hold=active`, bound to that bucket only) denies object access and bucket-policy changes to every other principal, including the deployer service account's project-wide `roles/storage.admin`. No WORM evidence writer runs as the deployer.
4. ✅ **`2026-11-15`–`2026-11-16`:** the 78 orphaned disks, the 78 temporary snapshots, and the 13 one-day-locked certification event buckets (`2026-11-10` to `2026-11-14`) were deleted `2026-11-15`, and all three unlocked Feb–Mar event buckets (`01c5a699`, `8c6c034e`, `687722bb`) were emptied and deleted `2026-11-16`.
5. ✅ **`2026-11-16`, `#780` (`775284e4`):** [`PRIVACY_IMPACT_ASSESSMENT.md`](../compliance/pia/PRIVACY_IMPACT_ASSESSMENT.md) (`v1.1`) adds a dated correction notice, retains the 90-day ceiling for non-audit conversational content, provides a complete store-by-store retention and enforceability inventory in `§6.2` (retired locked event bucket `2033-05-19`–`2033-10-27` asymmetry, disposed unlocked buckets, non-staging and staging event buckets, live operational trace stores for operational telemetry and not audit custody, gateway-mediated LangGraph checkpoints, educational query cache, 30-day application log stores for operational telemetry and not audit custody while authoritative audit custody exports to the `2555-day` locked WORM archive under `POAM-2026-197`, and governance Valkey defer tokens [working state, not audit custody] / KMS-signed WORM evidence chain), and withdraws the false `§6.2` NeMo trace-redaction claim in `§6.3`.
6. ✅ **`2026-11-15`, `#772` (`4ab01bb4`):** `POAM-2026-159`'s description of the bucket as operational telemetry is corrected by a dated note in that entry.
7. ✅ **`2026-11-16`, `#779` (`ae3e9b34`, `CP-1`, `POAM-2026-226`):** [`GatewayCheckpointStore`](../src/gateway/governance/checkpoint_store.py) and [`GatewayCheckpointSaver`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/checkpointer.py) enforce a server-derived TTL computed directly from `_DEFAULT_TTL` (`14,400 s` in [`defer_queue.py`](../src/gateway/governance/defer_queue.py)), `_DEFAULT_HOLD_TTL` (`300 s`), and [`resolve_hitl_approval_ttl_seconds()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/nodes/approval_node.py) (`300 s` default) plus a `60 s` park margin rounded up to whole minutes (`14,460 s` = `4h 1m`, capped by `CAGE_CHECKPOINT_MAX_TTL_SECONDS`, `90 d` hard ceiling), refreshed on writes only and never on reads, with `SHA-256`-hashed governance Valkey working-state key names (not audit custody) and body-only `thread_id` transport ([`test_gateway_checkpointer.py`](../tests/unit/test_gateway_checkpointer.py)).
8. ✅ **`2026-11-16` (`UP-1`, `#778` `fc7ac50a`):** `cage-staging` was re-applied on `ae3e9b34` in the 3-step `UP-1` sequence (`module.service_mesh` -> `module.cloudsql_postgres` + `module.langfuse` operational telemetry [not audit custody] + `langfuse_egress_l3_l4` -> `module.gateway` Helm swap + untargeted apply), restoring `governed-financial-advisor` (`2/2 Running`) with `0` post-apply Terraform drift changes (`No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration.`).

**Closure Criteria:**
1. ✅ Items 2 (`#774` `b12706d4`) and 7 (`#779` `ae3e9b34`) are merged, their tests pass on `main`, and the staging deployment is re-applied from Terraform (`UP-1` staged sequence on `ae3e9b34`), removing all drift and restoring the advisor on the post-fix image.
2. ✅ [`PRIVACY_IMPACT_ASSESSMENT.md`](../compliance/pia/PRIVACY_IMPACT_ASSESSMENT.md) (`v1.1`) provides the complete store inventory and actual enforceability, including the locked bucket's `2033` asymmetry, and withdraws the `§6.2` trace-redaction claim.

**Reopened (`2026-11-16`):** `#780` (`775284e4`) closed `POAM-2026-225` after inspecting only the sink-side modules (`defer_queue.py`, `stream.py`, `pii_sanitizer.py`), omitting the defer/evidence check from this entry and leaving caller-side paths unverified. Completing the end-to-end caller audit on `2026-11-16` established two results:
- **Defer tokens (`DEFER:*`, Valkey DB `0`, working state and not audit custody) — bounded within policy (`<= 4 h`):** [`_PARK_LUA`](../src/gateway/governance/defer_queue.py) atomically stamps `14,400 s` (`4 h`) or `300 s` (`5 min`) `EXPIRE` on every `DeferToken`, so `opa_input_snapshot` expires well inside both the resumption window and the 90-day ceiling.
- **Seven-year WORM evidence chain (`cage:evidence:stream` -> `module.worm_bucket`, locked `2,555 d`) — refusal-path leak (`RP-1`):** `GOVERNANCE_DECISION` ([`routing_seal.py`](../src/gateway/governance/routing_seal.py)), `GOVERNANCE_DEFERRAL` ([`verdicts.py`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/verdicts.py)), and `INFERENCE_PROXY_*` ([`inference_proxy.py`](../src/gateway/server/inference_proxy.py)) commit `params_hash` (`SHA-256`) or fixed rule reason strings only. However, [`build_refusal_receipt()`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/verdicts.py) and [`_emit_refusal_receipt()`](../src/gateway/server/governance_middleware.py) wrote raw `RefusalReceipt.attempted_params` into `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL` and `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL_RECEIPT`, while [`gateway_tool_guard`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/governance/tool_guard.py) forwarded unfiltered LLM `call["args"]` to `/governance/validate-action` and [`DoseOrder`](../src/cage_healthcare/tools/dose_order.py) passed `patient_id` and free-text clinical `indication`. [`PIISanitizer`](../src/gateway/governance/pii_sanitizer.py)'s regex patterns do not strip unlabelled prose or domain identifiers, so any free-text or identifier field on a refused call entered the 2,555-day locked archive.

**Remediation (reopened):**
9. ✅ **`2026-11-16`, `#781` (`87f4dca7`, `RP-1` in [`BREAKING_CHANGES.md`](BREAKING_CHANGES.md)):** [`refusal_projection.py`](../src/gateway/governance/refusal_projection.py) and [`RefusalReceipt`](../src/gateway/governance/contracts.py) schema `v4` (`to_worm_dict()`) split the 7-year WORM retention tier from the in-memory content tier: `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL`, `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL_RECEIPT`, and HTTP `403` `refusal_receipt` omit `attempted_params` unconditionally (enforced statically by [`check_producer_consumer_keys.py`](../scripts/check_producer_consumer_keys.py)) and record `params_hash` (`SHA-256`) plus `evaluated_params`, a default-deny projection constrained to closed `NUMBER`, `BOOLEAN`, `ENUM`, or `^[A-Z]{1,12}$` `UPPER_ALPHA_CODE` shapes on [`PluginContribution.evaluated_param_specs`](../src/gateway/governance/contracts.py) (a domain declaring nothing leaks nothing; identifier/credential/prose parameter names are rejected at assembly), while [`PRIVACY_IMPACT_ASSESSMENT.md`](../compliance/pia/PRIVACY_IMPACT_ASSESSMENT.md) `§6.2` documents the `v4` projection. Guarded by [`test_refusal_worm_projection.py`](../tests/unit/governance/test_refusal_worm_projection.py) and [`test_refusal_receipt_ingestion.py`](../tests/test_refusal_receipt_ingestion.py).
10. ✅ **`2026-11-16`, `#782` (`8a3e86bb`) & `#783` (`5d98e1e2`):** Live `cage-staging` rollout verification uncovered two mesh-policy issues blocking `governed-financial-advisor` `POST /governance/validate-action` calls: Linkerd `HTTPRoute/gateway-canary` (`#746`) matched `Exact POST /governance/{validate-action,policy-precheck}` ahead of `PathPrefix "/"` without binding `gateway-trusted-clients` (`HTTP 403` empty body for `cage-advisor-sa`), and `hashicorp/helm` did not hash local [`policy.yaml`](../infra/modules/gateway/mesh-policy/templates/policy.yaml) changes on `helm_release.mesh_policy`. `#782` bound `AuthorizationPolicy/gateway-canary-trusted` and enabled `canaryIdentities` in the `kind` Linkerd CI job, and `#783` added `templateSha256 = filesha256(...)` across all three local mesh-policy charts ([`test_gateway_mesh_policy.py`](../tests/test_gateway_mesh_policy.py)).
11. ✅ **`2026-11-16` (`cage-staging` live refusal & WORM stream read-back on `87f4dca7` + `#782`/`#783`):** All 6 first-party images built and attested in Cloud Build for `87f4dca7` and applied via `deploy_all.sh --target gcp-gke --env staging --image-sha=87f4dca7` (`0` post-apply drift). A live `POST /governance/validate-action` call from `governed-financial-advisor` (`cage-advisor-sa`) over Linkerd mTLS carrying canary identifier and free-text fields (`trader_id`, `rationale`, `notes`) returned `HTTP 403 DENIED` (`[STPA_UCA_UCA_6]`, `[FTRA_REGISTERED_IRREVERSIBLE]`) with `schema_version: "v4"`, `params_hash: "9e672a20...5d1562f"`, and bounded `evaluated_params` (`amount`, `confidence`, `daily_vol`, `drawdown`, `latency_ms`, `order_size`, `symbol`, `trader_role`) only; reading back `cage:evidence:stream` confirmed both `1794857433674-1` (`GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL`) and KMS-signed `1794857434281-0` (`GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL_RECEIPT`, `receipt_id: da825249-7af1-4731-9330-23d09ecc3d03`) carry `schema_version == "v4"`, `params_hash`, and bounded `evaluated_params` with `0` `attempted_params` keys and `0` canary bytes.

**Closure Criteria (reopened):**
3. ✅ Item 9 (`RP-1`) is squash-merged on `main` (`#781` `87f4dca7`, `48/48` CI checks green), along with `#782` (`8a3e86bb`) and `#783` (`5d98e1e2`).
4. ✅ `gateway` and `governed-financial-advisor` are rolled out on `cage-staging`, a refused governance call carrying canary free-text/identifier parameters is exercised over Linkerd mTLS against the live gateway, and reading back `cage:evidence:stream` (`1794857433674-1`, `1794857434281-0`) confirms `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL` and `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL_RECEIPT` contain `params_hash` and bounded `evaluated_params` only (zero `attempted_params` or canary bytes).

### POAM-2026-226: Advisor Checkpointer Silently Fell Back to Ephemeral Memory across Enforcing Postures

**Control:** NIST SC-24 (Fail in Known State), SI-10 (Information Input Validation), CA-7 (Continuous Monitoring)
**Risk Level:** High
**Status:** Closed (2026-11-16) — remediated in `#779` (`ae3e9b34`), `#781` (`87f4dca7`), `#782` (`8a3e86bb`), and `#783` (`5d98e1e2`), and verified live on `cage-staging`
**Owner:** Maintainer
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-16
**Target Closure:** 2026-11-30
**Date Closed:** 2026-11-16

**Description:**
[`get_checkpointer()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/checkpointer.py) fell back to LangGraph's in-process `MemorySaver` whenever Redis was unset, unreachable, or rejected `JSON.SET`, losing every paused HITL approval and deferred decision across pod restarts while advertising monitoring hooks that nothing read:
- **Unconsumed fallback hooks and blind `/health`:** `_set_memory_fallback_alerts()` logged a single startup `ERROR`, set `os.environ["CHECKPOINTER_TYPE"] = "memory"` and `_CHECKPOINTER_TYPE = "memory"`, and exposed `get_checkpointer_type()`. Neither `CHECKPOINTER_TYPE` nor `get_checkpointer_type()` had a single caller in `src/`, `infra/`, or `tests/`, no recording OTel span existed at startup to capture `checkpointer.memory_fallback`, `GET /health` in [`server.py`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/server.py) returned static `{"status": "ok"}`, and [`governed_advisor/main.tf`](../infra/modules/governed_advisor/main.tf) defined no readiness or liveness probes.
- **Staging network-policy and Valkey incompatibility:** [`gcp-gke/main.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/main.tf) wired `module.governed_advisor`'s `REDIS_HOST` to `module.memorystore_app`, while `financial-advisor-egress-internal-only` in [`network_policy.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/network_policy.tf) (`POAM-2026-195`: agents talk solely to `gateway`) granted `app_valkey_cidr` egress only to Langfuse. GKE Dataplane V2 policy-action logs recorded `deny` on `governed-financial-advisor -> 10.0.0.7:6379` and `:26379` (`2026-11-16T01:46Z`). Independently, `AsyncRedisSaver` (`langgraph-checkpoint-redis`) required `RedisJSON` (`JSON.SET`) and `RediSearch` (`FT.CREATE`), neither of which GCP Memorystore for Valkey provides, and `module.memorystore_app` ran with `persistence_mode = "DISABLED"` and `replica_count = 0` in `staging`. Every staging advisor boot since `2026-11-09` ran on `MemorySaver`.

**Remediation:**
1. ✅ **`2026-11-16`, `#779` (`ae3e9b34`, `CP-1` in [`BREAKING_CHANGES.md`](BREAKING_CHANGES.md)):** [`GatewayCheckpointStore`](../src/gateway/governance/checkpoint_store.py) and [`checkpoint_api.py`](../src/gateway/server/checkpoint_api.py) expose `/governance/checkpoints/{health,tuple,writes,get,list,delete}` on the gateway behind [`WorkloadIdentityMiddleware`](../src/gateway/server/workload_identity.py) (`l5d-client-id`), persisting opaque client-serialized checkpoints in logical DB `3` (`CAGE_CHECKPOINT_REDIS_DB`, working state and not audit custody) of `module.memorystore_governance` (AOF + replica durability, TLS, IAM auth) using standard Valkey commands (`HSET`, `HSETNX`, `ZADD`, `ZREVRANGEBYLEX`, `EXPIRE`, `DEL`) partitioned by `SHA-256(caller_identity)` with zero `network_policy.tf` egress exceptions (`POAM-2026-195` preserved).
2. ✅ **`2026-11-16`, `#779` (`ae3e9b34`, paired in the same PR so startup refusal never landed ahead of durable storage):** [`GatewayCheckpointSaver`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/checkpointer.py) and [`lifespan()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/server.py) refuse `MemorySaver` in every [`is_enforcing()`](../src/gateway/governance/env_posture.py) posture (`CheckpointDurabilityError`), verify `GET /governance/checkpoints/health` before serving traffic, report `checkpointer` and `durable` on `GET /health` (HTTP `503` when non-durable or unreachable), remove direct `REDIS_*` wiring from [`governed_advisor/main.tf`](../infra/modules/governed_advisor/main.tf) and [`gcp-gke/main.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/main.tf), and configure Kubernetes `/health` readiness and `/` liveness probes. Guarded by [`test_gateway_checkpointer.py`](../tests/unit/test_gateway_checkpointer.py), [`test_memorystore_topology.py`](../tests/infrastructure/test_memorystore_topology.py), and [`opa_uds_sidecar.tftest.hcl`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/tests/opa_uds_sidecar.tftest.hcl).
3. ✅ **`2026-11-16` (`cage-staging` live verification on `ae3e9b34`):** 3-step `UP-1` staging apply completed with `0` post-apply Terraform drift changes; `governed-financial-advisor` rolled out `2/2 Running` (`0` restarts) and `GET /health` returned `HTTP 200 {"status": "ok", "service": "financial-advisor-graph-agent", "checkpointer": "gateway", "durable": true, "checkpoint_ttl_seconds": 14460}`.

**Closure Criteria:**
1. ✅ Items 1 and 2 are squash-merged on `main` (`#779` `ae3e9b34`) with automated tests (`50/50` CI checks) and `.tftest.hcl` guards passing.
2. ✅ `staging` is re-applied (`0` drift) and `governed-financial-advisor` passes `/health` readiness with `"checkpointer": "gateway"` and `"durable": true`.

**Reopened (`2026-11-16`):** While `#779` (`ae3e9b34`) wired `readiness_probe` onto `GET /health` (which pings Redis DB `3` via `GET /governance/checkpoints/health` every `10 s` and pulls the pod after `3` failures), post-merge runtime audit of [`server.py`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/server.py) found two runtime defects inside the `0–30 s` window before kubelet marks the pod `NotReady` (or on direct pod calls):
- **Silent partial HITL queue (`87f4dca7^:src/governed_financial_advisor/server.py` `line 540`):** `list_pending_approvals()` wrapped per-thread `await graph.aget_state(config)` in `except Exception: continue`, returning `HTTP 200 {"pending": [...]}` silently omitting paused human-approval threads whenever the checkpoint store became unreachable mid-scan.
- **Generic `500` instead of `503`:** `query_agent()` (`require_thread_owner()` and `graph.ainvoke()`) and `list_pending_approvals()` wrapped `CheckpointDurabilityError` in generic `HTTP 500` rather than explicit `HTTP 503` (`checkpoint_store_unavailable`).

**Remediation (reopened):**
4. ✅ **`2026-11-16`, `#781` (`87f4dca7`):** [`server.py`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/server.py) removes the silent `except Exception: continue` in `list_pending_approvals()` and maps `CheckpointDurabilityError` to explicit `HTTP 503` (`{"error": "checkpoint_store_unavailable"}`) across `list_pending_approvals()` and `query_agent()`, guarded by [`test_gateway_checkpointer.py`](../tests/unit/test_gateway_checkpointer.py).
5. ✅ **`2026-11-16`, `#782` (`8a3e86bb`) & `#783` (`5d98e1e2`, `POAM-2026-227`):** Fixed `HTTPRoute/gateway-canary` route-precedence lockout of `cage-advisor-sa` on `POST /governance/{validate-action,policy-precheck}` via `AuthorizationPolicy/gateway-canary-trusted` and hashed local mesh-policy templates in `helm_release` ([`test_gateway_mesh_policy.py`](../tests/test_gateway_mesh_policy.py)).

**Closure Criteria (reopened):**
3. ✅ Item 4 is squash-merged on `main` (`#781` `87f4dca7`, `48/48` CI checks green) and rolled out on `cage-staging` alongside `#782`/`#783` (`0` post-apply drift), with `governed-financial-advisor` `2/2 Running` Ready (`GET /health` -> `HTTP 200 {"checkpointer": "gateway", "durable": true, "checkpoint_ttl_seconds": 14460}`) and `GET /v1/approvals/pending` verified live (`HTTP 200 {"pending": []}`).

### POAM-2026-227: Linkerd `HTTPRoute/gateway-canary` Route-Precedence Lockout Blocked `cage-advisor-sa` Governance Calls and `helm_release` Missed Local Template Edits

**Control:** NIST AC-3 (Access Enforcement), SC-7 (Boundary Protection), CA-7 (Continuous Monitoring), SA-11 (Developer Testing and Evaluation)
**Risk Level:** High (fail-closed governance routing outage, not bypass — caller audit below)
**Status:** Closed (2026-11-16) — remediated in `#782` (`8a3e86bb`) and `#783` (`5d98e1e2`), verified live on `cage-staging`
**Owner:** Maintainer
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-16
**Target Closure:** 2026-11-16
**Date Closed:** 2026-11-16

**Description:**
From `#746` (`f0ca9f4d`, merged `2026-11-14T11:08:18-05:00`) until `#782` (`8a3e86bb`) and `#783` (`5d98e1e2`) on `2026-11-16`, any cluster applying `main` with `enable_gateway_canary = true` (the default in [`variables.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/variables.tf)) rejected `governed-financial-advisor` (`cage-advisor-sa`) and every other `trusted_client_identities` workload at the Linkerd inbound proxy with empty-body `HTTP 403 Forbidden` (`Content-Length: 0`, `text/plain`) on `POST /governance/validate-action` and `POST /governance/policy-precheck`:
- **Gateway API / Linkerd route-precedence lockout (`#746` `f0ca9f4d`):** [`policy.yaml`](../infra/modules/gateway/mesh-policy/templates/policy.yaml) rendered `HTTPRoute/gateway-canary` matching `Exact POST /governance/validate-action` and `Exact POST /governance/policy-precheck` on `Server/gateway-http`. Under Gateway API specificity rules, an `Exact` path+method match supersedes `HTTPRoute/gateway-gated`'s `PathPrefix "/"` for all callers, and route-targeted `AuthorizationPolicy` grants do not inherit from less-specific routes. Because only `AuthorizationPolicy/gateway-canary` (`canaryIdentities`) targeted `HTTPRoute/gateway-canary` — and [`gateway/main.tf`](../infra/modules/gateway/main.tf) enforces `canary_client_identities ∩ trusted_client_identities == ∅` — Linkerd denied `cage-advisor-sa` before FastAPI ran.
- **Why CI missed it:** [`values.yaml`](../infra/modules/gateway/mesh-policy/values.yaml) sets `canaryIdentities: []`, so the `kind` Linkerd mesh-policy job in [`ci.yml`](../.github/workflows/ci.yml) skipped `{{- if .Values.canaryIdentities }}` and never rendered `HTTPRoute/gateway-canary` during live proxy verification.
- **Why Terraform missed `#782` until `#783`:** `hashicorp/helm` triggers an upgrade on a local directory chart (`chart = "${path.module}/mesh-policy"`) only when `Chart.yaml` `version` or rendered `values` change; editing `templates/*.yaml` alone produced `No changes` on existing clusters across [`gateway/main.tf`](../infra/modules/gateway/main.tf), [`compliance_bridge/main.tf`](../infra/modules/compliance_bridge/main.tf), and [`mesh_policy.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/mesh_policy.tf).
- **Caller-by-caller behavior during the window (fail-closed outage, zero governance bypass):**
  1. **[`CageClient._handle_deny_response()`](../packages/cage-client/src/cage_client/core.py) -> [`GatewayClient.validate_action()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/infrastructure/gateway_client.py):** On `HTTP 403` with `b""`, `response.json()` raised `json.JSONDecodeError`, which `_handle_deny_response()` wrapped as `CageGatewayError("Invalid JSON in DENY response: ...")`; [`_raise_unrouted()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/infrastructure/gateway_client.py) saw `response.status_code == 403` and raised `PermissionError("Governance DENIED '<action>': governance denied")`.
  2. **[`gateway_tool_guard()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/governance/tool_guard.py) (`authorize_action()`):** Caught `PermissionError`, returned `(None, reason)`, skipped the wrapped tool executor (`0` calls), cleared `routing_verdict_cache`, set `governance_status = "DENIED"`, and returned a refusal `ToolMessage`.
  3. **[`safety_check_node()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/nodes/safety_node.py) (`_route_trade()`):** Caught `PermissionError` and returned `"BLOCKED"` (clearing `routing_verdict_cache`). The misclassification of un-evidenced proxy/middleware `HTTP 403`s as `GOVERNANCE_DENIED` and the `consecutive_denials` increment on `GATEWAY_ERROR` are tracked as Open **`POAM-2026-228`** below.
  4. **[`GatewayClient.evaluate_policy_dry_run()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/infrastructure/gateway_client.py) (`POST /governance/policy-precheck`):** `response.raise_for_status()` raised `httpx.HTTPStatusError`, caught at `except Exception:` and returning `"DENY"`. Independently, [`evaluator_node()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/nodes/evaluator_node.py) routes dry-run previews via `POST /tools/execute` (`simulate_governance_check` on `HTTPRoute/gateway-gated`), and the single committing `SymbolicGovernor` + `verify_and_consume_seal()` run executes inside `gateway` on `POST /tools/execute`.
  5. **Live cluster window & WORM stream verification:** `cage-staging` Terraform state (`serial 737`) stayed at `2026-11-09` until the `2026-11-16` `UP-1` apply, so `HTTPRoute/gateway-canary` was active on `cage-staging` for ~2 hours on `2026-11-16` with zero external traffic before `#782` and `#783` rolled out. Live read-back of all `27` entries in `cage:evidence:stream` (`1794199857640-0` through `1794857434281-0`) confirmed `0` `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL` or `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL_RECEIPT` entries between `2026-11-09T17:36:40Z` and the post-`#783` `2026-11-16T19:30:33Z` verification probe (`1794857433674-1` / `1794857434281-0`).

**Remediation:**
1. ✅ **`2026-11-16`, `#782` (`8a3e86bb`):** [`policy.yaml`](../infra/modules/gateway/mesh-policy/templates/policy.yaml) binds `AuthorizationPolicy/gateway-canary-trusted` (`gateway-trusted-clients`) onto `HTTPRoute/gateway-canary`, [`ci.yml`](../.github/workflows/ci.yml) deploys `gateway-mesh-policy` in the `kind` Linkerd job with non-empty `canaryIdentities` and verifies `advisor -> POST /governance/validate-action` does not return a mesh `403`, and [`test_gateway_mesh_policy.py`](../tests/test_gateway_mesh_policy.py) fails if any `HTTPRoute` on `gateway-http` shadows `PathPrefix "/"` without granting `gateway-trusted-clients`.
2. ✅ **`2026-11-16`, `#783` (`5d98e1e2`):** [`gateway/main.tf`](../infra/modules/gateway/main.tf), [`compliance_bridge/main.tf`](../infra/modules/compliance_bridge/main.tf), and [`mesh_policy.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/mesh_policy.tf) inject `templateSha256 = filesha256(...)` into `helm_release` `values` (guarded statically in [`test_gateway_mesh_policy.py`](../tests/test_gateway_mesh_policy.py)).
3. ✅ **`2026-11-16`, `#785` (`00a1c461`):** `TestLinkerdEmpty403FailsClosed` in [`test_gateway_tool_guard.py`](../tests/test_gateway_tool_guard.py) replays empty-body `HTTP 403` (`text/plain`) across `GatewayClient.validate_action()`, `gateway_tool_guard()`, `safety_check_node()`, and `GatewayClient.evaluate_policy_dry_run()`; live `cage-staging` rollout on `87f4dca7` + `#782`/`#783` (`0` post-apply drift) verified `AuthorizationPolicy/gateway-canary-trusted` present in `governance-stack` and end-to-end `cage-advisor-sa -> POST /governance/validate-action` routing over Linkerd mTLS.

**Closure Criteria:**
1. ✅ `#782` (`8a3e86bb`) and `#783` (`5d98e1e2`) are squash-merged on `main` and applied on `cage-staging` with `0` drift and live `cage-advisor-sa -> POST /governance/validate-action` mTLS verification.
2. ✅ [`test_gateway_mesh_policy.py`](../tests/test_gateway_mesh_policy.py) and [`test_gateway_tool_guard.py`](../tests/test_gateway_tool_guard.py) bind `POAM-2026-227` and verify both the mesh-policy/Helm contracts and fail-closed advisor behavior on empty-body `HTTP 403`.

**Correction (`2026-11-16`, `POAM-2026-231` / `POAM-2026-230`):** During the lockout window on `cage-staging`, neither `#746` alarm (`gateway_sustained_refusal_ratio` nor `gateway_zero_permitted_requests`) could detect the advisor lockout: Linkerd `403`s stopped at `:4143` before `WorkloadIdentityMiddleware`, the canary itself could not boot (`CAGE_DEPLOYMENT_REGION` unset; `POAM-2026-231` Finding 3), and had the canary run its admitted probes would have kept `rate(permitted) > 0` while all alarms lacked a notification channel (`POAM-2026-230`).

### POAM-2026-228: Advisor Misclassifies Un-Evidenced Proxy/Middleware `HTTP 403`s as Policy Denials and Increments `consecutive_denials` on `GATEWAY_ERROR`

**Control:** NIST SI-10 (Information Input Validation), SC-24 (Fail in Known State), AU-3 (Content of Audit Records), CA-7 (Continuous Monitoring)
**Risk Level:** Moderate (fail-closed execution holds; blast-radius check below confirms zero WORM evidence-chain or gateway policy-refusal counter corruption)
**Status:** Open
**Owner:** Maintainer
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-16
**Target Closure:** 2026-11-30

**Description:**
Caller and downstream-surface analysis of `POAM-2026-227` uncovered coupled advisor, attestation, and formal-model error-classification defects across `src/governed_financial_advisor/`, `src/integrations/provider_02/adapter.py`, and [`LangGraphHarness.tla`](../proof/LangGraphHarness.tla):
1. **Bypass of `CageClient`'s refusal-authenticity check & un-evidenced policy-drift replay (`gateway_client.py`):** Every real policy refusal from `POST /governance/validate-action` ([`governance_middleware.py`](../src/gateway/server/governance_middleware.py)) is an `HTTP 403` JSON payload carrying `proof_hash` (and `refusal_receipt`), which [`CageClient._handle_deny_response()`](../packages/cage-client/src/cage_client/core.py) validates before raising `PolicyViolationException`; any non-JSON `403` (Linkerd inbound sidecar empty-body `403`, upstream proxy `403`) or `proof_hash`-less `403` ([`WorkloadIdentityMiddleware`](../src/gateway/server/workload_identity.py) `403 {"detail": "Forbidden..."}`) raises `CageGatewayError`. However, [`_raise_unrouted()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/infrastructure/gateway_client.py) converted every `status_code == 403` `CageGatewayError` into `PermissionError("Governance DENIED ...")`, [`_route_trade()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/nodes/safety_node.py) duplicated that branch on `httpx.HTTPStatusError` (`status_code == 403`) -> `reason_code="GOVERNANCE_DENIED"`, `recoverable=True`, and [`_is_policy_drift()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/infrastructure/gateway_client.py) in [`_AdvisorTransport.handle_async_request()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/infrastructure/gateway_client.py) triggered a `GET /governance/policy-version` pin refresh and trade preview replay whenever any `403` body contained `"Substrate Policy Drift Detected"` without checking for a non-empty `proof_hash` or `audit_id`.
2. **Four human, operational, and latent downstream surfaces polluted by `GATEWAY_ERROR` → `BLOCKED` / `consecutive_denials + 1`:** Because [`_blocked()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/nodes/safety_node.py) (mirrored in [`LangGraphHarness.tla`](../proof/LangGraphHarness.tla) `SafetyDeny`) incremented `consecutive_denials` on `GATEWAY_ERROR` (`500`, `401`, `ReadTimeout`, `ConnectError`, and un-evidenced `403`s) and reported `safety_status = "BLOCKED"` / `"HARD_PAUSE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED"`:
   - **Surface A — `POST /agent/query` user-facing reply ([`explainer_node()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/nodes/explainer_node.py)):** Two transient mesh/gateway failures tripped `consecutive_denials >= MAX_CONSECUTIVE_DENIALS` (`2`), causing `explainer_node()` to return a false policy-probing accusation (`"This request has been denied 2 consecutive times by the governance system... To prevent policy-probing attacks"`), or even on a single failure when prior denials existed on the thread.
   - **Surface B — 30-day Cloud Logging operational `ERROR` records (`safety_node.py` / `explainer_node.py`, non-custody operational logs, not WORM audit evidence):** Un-evidenced `403`s logged `"Action DENIED by governance"` and repeated gateway faults logged `"MAX_CONSECUTIVE_DENIALS exceeded"`, conflating infrastructure outages with policy violations in 30-day operational logs.
   - **Surface C — [`query_agent()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/server.py) `QueryCache` guard (`server.py`):** Despite the comment `# Blocked responses are not cached`, `server.py` gated `await query_cache.set(...)` solely on `not (res and res.get("guardrail_blocked"))`, leaving non-approved `safety_status` turns (`GATEWAY_ERROR`, `BLOCKED`, `DEFERRED`, `HARD_PAUSE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `ESCALATED`) eligible for caching if a prompt matched a cacheable category.
   - **Surface D — [`Provider02AttestationCallback`](../src/integrations/provider_02/adapter.py) terminal-path classification ([`adapter.py`](../src/integrations/provider_02/adapter.py)):** [`_classify_terminal_path()`](../src/integrations/provider_02/adapter.py) mapped `safetyStatus == "BLOCKED"` unconditionally to `"cbf_block"` (and without a `GATEWAY_ERROR` guard would fall through `evaluator` + `explainer` to `"loop_breaker"`), mislabeling gateway transport/verification failures in Provider 02 attestation bundles.
3. **Verified blast radius & scope boundary (why `Moderate`, and what this split does not cover):**
   - **Advisor/sidecar stream boundary (`2026-11-16`, qualified):** `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL` ([`verdicts.py`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/verdicts.py)) and `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL_RECEIPT` ([`governance_middleware.py`](../src/gateway/server/governance_middleware.py)) are emitted exclusively inside `gateway` (`Layer 1`) — never by `governed_financial_advisor`, Linkerd (`:4143`), or `WorkloadIdentityMiddleware`. Live read-back of all `27` entries in `cage-staging` `cage:evidence:stream` (`2026-11-16`) showed `0` false refusal records across `2026-11-09`–`2026-11-16`. **Qualification (`2026-11-16`):** that `0`-of-`27` figure is an empirical count over low-volume synthetic traffic, **not** a structural guarantee that the evidence chain is free of false refusals.
   - **Boundary statement (`2026-11-16`):** This advisor-side split (`POAM-2026-228`) prevents client-side misclassification of un-evidenced `403`s and transport failures. It **cannot** detect or prevent false refusals that the gateway itself signs with a valid `proof_hash` when an internal gateway dependency fails (for example, OPA unreachable collapsed to `"DENY"` in `PolicyClient`, or Redis/provider errors mapped to `HARD` violations). Those gateway-signed false attestations satisfy `CageClient._handle_deny_response()` and enter the WORM chain, advisor denial budget, refusal-ratio metric, and HITL approval spend; they are tracked separately in **`POAM-2026-233`**.
   - **Gateway refusal metrics (`#746`, qualified `2026-11-16`):** Linkerd sidecar `403`s stop at `:4143` before `WorkloadIdentityMiddleware` (`:8080`), incrementing neither `cage_gateway_gated_requests_total{outcome="blocked"}` nor `cage_governance_refusals_total{tier}` ([`metrics.py`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/metrics.py)). Inside `gateway`, `WorkloadIdentityMiddleware` counts non-open `http_status >= 400` responses under `cage_gateway_gated_requests_total{outcome="blocked"}`; note that `gateway_sustained_refusal_ratio` ([`metrics_alerting.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/metrics_alerting.tf)) had `notification_channels = []` until `POAM-2026-230` closed on `2026-11-23` (`#859` `fc0152a8` + `#862` `5fa41805`) and `cage_gateway_gated_requests_total` remains subject to the `DEFER`/canary counting bias (`POAM-2026-231`).

**Remediation (Implemented in code `2026-11-16` on `fix/advisor-gateway-error-split`; Open pending mainline squash-merge SHA):**
1. ✅ **Refusal-authenticity & policy-drift replay gating ([`gateway_client.py`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/infrastructure/gateway_client.py)):** Removed the `status_code == 403 -> PermissionError` collapse in [`_raise_unrouted()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/infrastructure/gateway_client.py) so un-evidenced `403`s re-raise `httpx.HTTPStatusError` (and unsigned `200`/`202` bodies raise `CageGatewayError`), and gated [`_is_policy_drift()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/infrastructure/gateway_client.py) in [`_AdvisorTransport.handle_async_request()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/infrastructure/gateway_client.py) on non-empty `proof_hash` / `refusal_receipt.proof_hash` / `audit_id` ([`test_policy_pinning.py`](../tests/test_policy_pinning.py)).
2. ✅ **First-class `safety_status = "GATEWAY_ERROR"` & invariant `consecutive_denials` ([`state.py`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/state.py), [`agent_state_schema.json`](../compliance/schemas/agent_state_schema.json), [`safety_node.py`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/nodes/safety_node.py)):** Added `"GATEWAY_ERROR"` to [`AgentState`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/state.py), removed the `status_code == 403 -> GOVERNANCE_DENIED` fallback in [`_route_trade()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/nodes/safety_node.py), introduced [`_gateway_error()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/nodes/safety_node.py) keeping `consecutive_denials` unchanged (`recoverable=False`) and logging `"Gateway validation unavailable/unverified — failing closed"` at `ERROR`, and routed `GATEWAY_ERROR` to `"explainer"` in [`route_safety()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/nodes/safety_node.py).
3. ✅ **Downstream human, cache, and attestation guards ([`explainer_node.py`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/nodes/explainer_node.py), [`server.py`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/server.py), [`adapter.py`](../src/integrations/provider_02/adapter.py)):** [`explainer_node()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/nodes/explainer_node.py) checks `safety_status == "GATEWAY_ERROR"` ahead of `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_DENIALS` to return a deterministic fail-closed infrastructure message without LLM calls or policy-probing claims; [`query_agent()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/server.py) caches only when `not guardrail_blocked` and `safety_status in (None, "APPROVED", "SKIPPED")`; and [`_extract_signals()`](../src/integrations/provider_02/adapter.py) / [`_classify_terminal_path()`](../src/integrations/provider_02/adapter.py) classify `GATEWAY_ERROR` steps as `"unknown"` rather than `"cbf_block"`.
4. ✅ **Formal specification split ([`LangGraphHarness.tla`](../proof/LangGraphHarness.tla), [`tla_pins.py`](../proof/tla_pins.py)):** Added `"GATEWAY_ERROR"` to `SafetyStatuses` and `RefusedTurnNeverTrades`, and split `SafetyTransportError` (`UNCHANGED consecutive_denials`, `UNCHANGED evidence_committed`) from `SafetyDeny`, verified by TLC v1.7.4 (`83,729` distinct states, `0` invariant violations on `LangGraphHarness.cfg`; `915` distinct states violating `SingleUseDeferralTicket` on `LangGraphHarness_unguarded.cfg`).
5. ✅ **Cryptographic HTTP `403` refusal verification & `cage-client v0.4.0` (`2026-11-19`, `#820` `3feffdf6`, `CC-04`, `GHSA-gc2v-v2jw-q499`):** [`governance_middleware.py`](../src/gateway/server/governance_middleware.py) wraps HTTP `403 DENIED` refusals in a signed `GovernanceEnvelope` (failing closed with `503` `envelope_signing_unavailable` if signing fails), `cage-client v0.4.0` ([`core.py`](../packages/cage-client/src/cage_client/core.py)) verifies both `200` and `403` identically via `_verify_envelope_response()` and removes unsigned `202`/`409`/`422` mediation, and [`GatewayClient.validate_action()`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/infrastructure/gateway_client.py) runs `_is_policy_drift()` replay only after `CageClient` authenticates the `403` envelope. **Procedural disclosure-order gap (`2026-11-19`):** PR `#820` (`fix/cage-client-verify-verdicts`) was pushed and opened publicly (`20:15Z`) ~6 minutes before `GHSA-gc2v-v2jw-q499` was published (`20:21Z`), inverting `SECURITY.md`'s publish-first `T=0` sequence while `#820` was open. Practical exposure during that window was minimal (`cage-client` is not on PyPI, `v0.3.0` was primarily CI-fetched, and exploitation required an on-path intermediary across Linkerd mTLS); `GHSA-gc2v-v2jw-q499` was published before `#820` merged (`3feffdf6`) and [`SECURITY.md`](../SECURITY.md) now states explicit applicability rules for the `T=0` flow.

**Closure Criteria:**
1. Un-evidenced `HTTP 403`s (empty mesh `403`, `WorkloadIdentityMiddleware` `403`, proxy `403` without `proof_hash`/`audit_id`, including spoofed policy-drift `403`s) classify as `GATEWAY_ERROR` (`recoverable=False`) without policy-pin refresh/replay, never `GOVERNANCE_DENIED`, verified in [`test_poam_228_gateway_error_split.py`](../tests/unit/test_poam_228_gateway_error_split.py), [`test_policy_pinning.py`](../tests/test_policy_pinning.py), [`test_safety_node.py`](../tests/test_safety_node.py), [`test_gateway_tool_guard.py`](../tests/test_gateway_tool_guard.py), and [`test_trade_contract.py`](../tests/test_trade_contract.py).
2. `GATEWAY_ERROR` leaves `consecutive_denials` unchanged, emits no false policy-probing reply in `explainer_node()`, is excluded from `QueryCache` and `provider_02` `"cbf_block"` classification, and passes TLC model checking (`LangGraphHarness.tla` `SafetyTransportError`, [`test_tla_specs_proof.py`](../tests/test_tla_specs_proof.py)) on the squash-merged mainline commit.

### POAM-2026-230: No Alert Reaches Anyone: Cloud Monitoring Policies Have No Notification Channel and the Compliance-Bridge Notifier Writes Only Log Lines

**Control:** NIST SI-4 (System Monitoring), AU-5 (Response to Audit Logging Process Failures), AU-12 (Audit Record Generation), CA-7 (Continuous Monitoring), IR-4 (Incident Handling), IR-6 (Incident Reporting), ISO/IEC 42001 A.5.3 (Logging and Monitoring)
**Risk Level:** Moderate, rated on the impact window below. The defect alone would rate High (basis below), and this item rises to High if, before it closes, a deployment carrying non-synthetic traffic is made from a committed profile or any closure, certification, attestation or release note cites these alerts as reaching a responder
**Status:** Closed
**Owner:** Maintainer (`infra/targets/gcp-gke` alerting)
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-16
**Target Closure:** 2026-11-30
**Date Closed:** 2026-11-23

**Description:**
Every Cloud Monitoring alert policy CAGE creates sets `notification_channels = var.lula_alert_notification_channels`: [`lula_alerting.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/lula_alerting.tf) L29 and L82, and [`metrics_alerting.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/metrics_alerting.tf) L97, L189, L246, L299, L354 and L420. The variable ([`variables.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/variables.tf) L788–792) is a `list(string)` with `default = []` and no validation, and its description says it is attached to "the Lula compliance audit AlertPolicy" although all eight policies use it. None of the eight committed profiles (`dev`, `staging`, `prod`, `eu-dev`, `eu-prod`, `apac-dev`, `apac-prod`, `us-dev`) sets it, nor does [`terraform.auto.tfvars.example`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/terraform.auto.tfvars.example), [`gen_tfvars.py`](../scripts/gen_tfvars.py) or any workflow. Each policy is counted on `local.enforcing_posture` ([`main.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/main.tf) L229), so the six enforcing profiles (`staging`, `prod`, `eu-prod` and `apac-prod`, plus `eu-dev` and `apac-dev` through `enforce_in_dev = true`) create all eight policies with no recipient, and `dev` and `us-dev` create none. When a condition holds, Cloud Monitoring opens an incident and tells no one.

**The compliance-bridge notifier (folded in `2026-11-16`):** The reference Terraform passes `alert_channel = "console"` ([`main.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/main.tf) L937; present in root commit `1902c92c`, `2026-06-01`, so git cannot date it earlier) to the bridge's `ALERT_CHANNEL` ([`compliance_bridge/main.tf`](../infra/modules/compliance_bridge/main.tf) L286–289). [`create_notifier()`](../src/compliance_bridge/notifier.py) defaults to the console (L669) and falls back to it with only a warning when `pagerduty`, `webhook` or `slack` lacks its secret (L671–704). Every emitter therefore writes a log line: critical Lula `FAIL` or `ERROR` findings ([`audit_workflow.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/audit_workflow.py) L393–394), `lula_audit` infrastructure events ([`main.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/main.py) L1490–1491), and evidence-age and dead-man breaches ([`sla_monitor.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/sla_monitor.py) L211, L294). `_step4_alert_on_critical_fail()` then returns `True`, recorded as alerted, after the console write (L396–400). The SSP, the SP 800-53 profile, the active `lula-validation-ir6.yaml` and several documents describe Slack and PagerDuty delivery that no committed profile configures. It fails the same four properties as the Cloud Monitoring policies, so it is folded into this item rather than split into one that could only close with it.

**Why the control looked operational:**
1. **The owner label is not a recipient.** Each policy sets the `owner` user label from `lula_alert_owner` (default `platform-compliance-oncall`) and prints it as "Owner" in its documentation. A label routes nothing. The variable's description ("Named on-call team or owner label responsible for triaging Lula compliance audit alerts") and the header comment of `lula_alerting.tf` ("pages the named owner") describe routing that no resource performs.
2. **The tests prove propagation of a value no profile supplies.** CI runs `terraform test -var-file=staging.tfvars` (job `terraform-test` in [`ci.yml`](../.github/workflows/ci.yml)). In [`lula_cron.tftest.hcl`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/tests/lula_cron.tftest.hcl), run `staging_plans_lula_cron_active_specs_and_dedicated_ksas` asserts that the staging profile plans all eight policies with the `owner` label and asserts nothing about channels, so CI passes the exact posture that routes nowhere. Run `custom_lula_alert_owner_and_channels_propagate` (L240–275) supplies a test channel and proves that a supplied channel reaches all eight policies; no committed profile supplies one, and nothing requires one.
3. **Commit messages, the changelog and a release body said the alerts reach someone.** Commit messages cannot be edited, so the strike is recorded here: `#704` (`600de728`) describes its change as wiring alerting through a "Cloud Monitoring AlertPolicy with named lula_alert_owner", and `#746` (`f0ca9f4d`) provisions the refusal-ratio policy "to page lula_alert_owner" and the zero-permitted policy so an outage "continues paging after upstream callers stop retrying". Neither policy pages anyone. The `v4.1.0` entry in [`CHANGELOG.md`](../CHANGELOG.md), repeated verbatim in the `v4.1.0` GitHub release body, describes the dead-man's switch alert policy as bound to a named maintainer's account; it is bound to no channel. The changelog carries a dated correction; the release body is a maintainer edit (closure criterion 5).

**Defect window, per policy** (each policy's adding commit from `git log -S` on its resource address, `origin/main`):

| `google_monitoring_alert_policy` | Display name (after the cluster-name prefix) | Added in | Window opens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lula_audit_failure` | Lula Compliance Audit Failure / Dead-Man Switch (A.5.3) | `#704` (`600de728`), with both variables | `2026-11-09` |
| `lula_audit_pod_restart` | Lula Compliance Auditor Pod Restart (A.5.3) | `#708` (`455aa1ba`), split out of `lula_audit_failure` because Cloud Monitoring rejects multi-condition PromQL policies | `2026-11-09` |
| `prometheus_metrics_scrape_liveness` | GMP Metrics Scrape & Series Arrival Down / Absent (AU-12) | `#733` (`88015ad8`) | `2026-11-13` |
| `gateway_sustained_refusal_ratio` | Gateway Sustained Refusal Ratio >= 95% (SI-4 / AU-5) | `#746` (`f0ca9f4d`) | `2026-11-14` |
| `gateway_zero_permitted_requests` | Gateway Zero Permitted Gated Requests for 15m (SI-4 / AU-5) | `#746` (`f0ca9f4d`) | `2026-11-14` |
| `gateway_canary_probe_absent` | Gateway Synthetic Canary Probes Absent for 5m (SI-4 / CA-7) | `#746` (`f0ca9f4d`) | `2026-11-14` |
| `gateway_canary_pod_health` | Gateway Synthetic Canary Pod Restart / Eviction (SI-4 / CA-7) | `#746` (`f0ca9f4d`) | `2026-11-14` |
| `gateway_evidence_append_reconciliation` | Gateway Permitted Traffic vs Evidence Appends Deficit (AU-5 / AU-12) | `#749` (`05275d02`) | `2026-11-14` |

Every window is still open at `c5de2555`. The defect is in committed configuration, so it covers every enforcing committed profile, `prod` included.

**Impact window (realised exposure):** No production deployment of CAGE exists, so the defect is realised only where an enforcing profile was applied, all of it carrying synthetic traffic only:
1. `cage-staging`, read live on `2026-11-16` at about 23:20Z: all eight policies exist and are enabled, each with `0` notification channels, and the project holds `0` notification channels of any type.
2. The two Gate W clean-room projects, which the Gate W lifecycle script named in [`gate_w_certification.json`](../compliance/gate_w_certification.json) deploys in the staging environment from `staging.tfvars`. By commit ancestry against each policy's adding commit, `fa772122` (`v4.1.0`, `2026-11-12`) carried `lula_audit_failure` and `lula_audit_pod_restart`, and `8956f505` (certified `2026-11-14T01:59:25Z`) carried those two and `prometheus_metrics_scrape_liveness`, none with a channel.

This record does not establish whether any policy opened an incident in those projects during its window; remediation item 5 reads it back for `cage-staging`, and for each Gate W project that still exists.

**Realised (`2026-11-16`):** The finding is not latent. Two real control failures held their alert conditions on `cage-staging` and nobody was notified; both were found only because an agent looked:
1. **The canary has not completed a probe.** Neither of its ReplicaSets (created `2026-11-16T15:28:12Z` and `18:10:50Z`) has had a pod complete a probe (operator read-back, `2026-11-16`). The container exits with `DeploymentRegionError` (`CAGE_DEPLOYMENT_REGION is not set`) before the probe loop: `#764` (`3347b4b1`, `2026-11-15`) made the region mandatory under an enforcing posture, and [`gateway_canary.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/gateway_canary.tf) sets `CAGE_ENV` (L119) but not the region. Read back with `kubectl` at about `2026-11-17T00:27Z`: the current pod, created `23:19:48Z`, had restarted 14 times and its previous container logged that error. `gateway_canary_probe_absent` and `gateway_canary_pod_health` have held their conditions since about 15:30Z (`POAM-2026-231`).
2. **`lula-audit` has failed every run since the `2026-11-16` deploy — compounded by restart-extended startup grace.** Runs at `15:15Z`, `18:00Z` and `2026-11-17T00:00Z` failed; the CronJob's last success is `2026-11-09T06:15:38Z`. The `00:00Z` run logged `24/26 satisfied (2 failed: lula-validation-a53,lula-validation-aarm-vectors)` (diagnosed as `empty_audit_evidence`, `0` records). `lula_audit_failure` held its condition with no recipient. Independently, compliance-bridge pod restarts at `15:01Z`, `15:28Z`, and `18:10Z` reset `_DEPLOYMENT_START_UTC` and re-armed the 6h `STARTUP_GRACE_HOURS` window across 9h (`15:01Z`–`00:12Z`), silencing [`_check_lula_audit_deadman()`](../src/compliance_bridge/sla_monitor.py) throughout the same window (`POAM-2026-234`). Even with a notification channel wired, the Lula dead-man would not have paged — two independent failures in the alarm path, not one.

**Why it matters:** These eight policies are the detection-and-response leg CAGE claims for SI-4, AU-5, CA-7 and ISO 42001 A.5.3, and AU-5 requires alerting designated personnel when audit logging fails. Every alarm discussed in `POAM-2026-228`, and every canary alarm the planned canary item will add or repair, reaches no one whatever the canary's state: repairing the canary restores the signal, not the notification. The break-glass procedure in [`GKE_TEST_RUNBOOK.md`](operations/GKE_TEST_RUNBOOK.md), which turns `EVIDENCE_CHAIN_BLOCKING` off, tells the operator that `gateway_evidence_append_reconciliation` pages; under break-glass that alarm is the only detection of permitted traffic without durable appends. Enforcement does not depend on these alarms: evidence-chain blocking, single-use seal consumption and governance refusals fail closed in code. The alarms detect failures that already fail closed, which leaves an outage silent rather than unsafe, or failures under break-glass, which they leave undetected.

**Severity basis:**
- **Defect window (would rate High alone).** It has the shape of `POAM-2026-221` (High): a control that reported itself operational while doing nothing. There, CI gates were green while checking nothing; here, eight `CRITICAL` policies are enabled while notifying no one, with an owner label, a propagation test and commit messages vouching for them. In every committed profile, `prod` included, the response leg of AU-5, SI-4 and IR-4 does not exist.
- **Impact window (Moderate).** Unlike `POAM-2026-221`, whose gates ran on every merge to `main` for up to five and a half months, this defect is realised only in one staging environment and two ephemeral certification projects carrying synthetic traffic, from `2026-11-09` at the earliest. Enforcement fails closed without the alarms; what is lost is timely detection of degraded operation. That is the class of `POAM-2026-222` (Moderate: monitoring that does not exist, with no executed reliance on it) and `POAM-2026-224` (Moderate: an assurance artefact that claimed more than it checked).
- **Raised to High** if either condition in the risk level occurs before closure.
- **The realised impact against those conditions (`2026-11-16`).** Neither condition is met: both failures occurred on staging, which carries synthetic traffic only, and no closure, certification, attestation or release note now cites these alerts as reaching a responder (this record corrects the ones that did). The rating stays Moderate, but not as a latent defect: the cost the Moderate basis names, timely detection of degraded operation, was paid twice on one day.

**Dependencies:** The planned canary item (`POAM-2026-231`) and fiscal `UNKNOWN`-resolution item (`POAM-2026-232`) both depend on this one: any alarm they add or repair routes nowhere until it closes, so neither may close on an alarm before this item does.

**Remediation (separate PR; this record changes no Terraform or code):**
1. Rename `lula_alert_notification_channels` and `lula_alert_owner` to their real scope, every alert policy in the target, with descriptions that say what each is: the channel set, and a label that routes nothing.
2. Provision the staging channel out-of-band as a type whose destination the check can read, decided when it is provisioned rather than retrofitted: a Pub/Sub topic, or a webhook with a readable sink. Email or paging fans out behind it and is not bound directly. Its resource name lives only in the gitignored `terraform.auto.tfvars`, and [`terraform.auto.tfvars.example`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/terraform.auto.tfvars.example) shows a `<PROJECT_ID>` / `<CHANNEL_ID>` placeholder.
3. Add a dedicated heartbeat alert policy whose documentation and labels say it is a heartbeat needing no action. The recurring check trips only the heartbeat, never a real policy: a scheduled page from a real alarm teaches responders to ignore that alarm.
4. Correct the Terraform comments and `documentation` strings that say the policies page: `lula_alerting.tf` L19, and `metrics_alerting.tf` L58, L158, L165–166, L211, L272, L443 and L454. They are Terraform, which this record does not change.
5. Read back each policy's incident history over its window on `cage-staging`, and on each Gate W project that still exists, and record the result here. An incident opened with no channel is an alarm nobody saw; any found is triaged and cited.
6. For the notifier: enforce property 1b at bridge start, record `alerted` from observed delivery rather than from the call ([`audit_workflow.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/audit_workflow.py) L396–400), and correct `lula-validation-ir6.yaml` L21 and L46. This record does not edit that spec: it is mounted into the active Lula ConfigMap, so editing it changes deployed content.

**Closure Criteria:** Four properties, each necessary and none a substitute for another (property 1 has a Terraform-channel form and an application-config form), plus the corrections and the read-back. Presence at plan time and delivery at run time are different properties: a plan can carry a channel ID that no longer resolves, and an existing, enabled channel can deliver to a dead destination.
1. ✅ **Met — Plan-time validity.** Every channel in the bound set exists and is enabled when the plan runs (`data.google_monitoring_notification_channel.bound` in [`alert_routing.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/alert_routing.tf)), enforced by a `lifecycle` `precondition` on each of the `9` `google_monitoring_alert_policy` resources (never a variable validation or standalone `terraform_data` guard), with `expect_failures` runs in [`lula_cron.tftest.hcl`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/tests/lula_cron.tftest.hcl) (`13/13` passed) for an empty set, a missing channel, and a disabled channel in an enforcing posture.
   ✅ **Met — 1b. Start-time validity, for application alert config.** In an enforcing posture (`kubernetes_deployment.compliance_bridge` `lifecycle` `precondition` in [`compliance_bridge/main.tf`](../infra/modules/compliance_bridge/main.tf) + `validate_notifier_config()` in [`notifier.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/notifier.py) + `lifespan()` in [`main.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/main.py)), `compliance-bridge` fails closed with `NotifierConfigError` when `ALERT_CHANNEL` is unset, is `console`, or lacks its destination (`14/14` runs in [`operator_identity.tftest.hcl`](../infra/modules/compliance_bridge/tests/operator_identity.tftest.hcl) + [`test_compliance_notifier_routing.py`](../tests/unit/test_compliance_notifier_routing.py)).
2. ✅ **Met — Bindings, at plan time and at run time.** Every `google_monitoring_alert_policy` in the target (`9/9`, including `alert_pipeline_heartbeat` over `google_monitoring_metric_descriptor.alert_heartbeat_probe`) binds `local.resolved_alert_notification_channels`, verified at plan time in [`lula_cron.tftest.hcl`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/tests/lula_cron.tftest.hcl) and at run time by `verify_runtime_alert_policies()` in [`verify_alert_delivery.py`](../scripts/verify_alert_delivery.py) (`policy_count == 9`, exact set equality). Every application alert emitter in [`audit_workflow.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/audit_workflow.py), [`main.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/main.py), and [`sla_monitor.py`](../src/compliance_bridge/sla_monitor.py) routes through `PubSubNotifier` and records `alerted` / `remediation_sent` strictly from observed `(await notifier.send_*(...)) is True`.
3. ✅ **Met — Delivery, observed at the destination (amended `2026-11-22` — Reference-Architecture Terminal Sink).** Because CAGE is a reference architecture demonstrating AI governance patterns rather than a deployed production service, GCP Cloud Pub/Sub (`topics/cage-staging-alerts` → `subscriptions/cage-staging-alerts-verify`) is the **terminal destination by design** for both Cloud Monitoring `AlertPolicy` resources and `PubSubNotifier` (personal email, SMS, and commercial paging fan-out beyond Pub/Sub are out of scope / adopter-operated by design). Both envelopes — Cloud Monitoring `alert_pipeline_heartbeat` incident notifications and the live `compliance-bridge` pod's `source == "compliance-bridge"` / `alert_type == "heartbeat"` messages — were pulled and verified directly at `subscriptions/cage-staging-alerts-verify` locally (`2026-11-22T23:28:41Z`, `0.ofbr7ked883k` + `notifier-heartbeat-17c02283699c` `message_id=23431802309079337`) and across back-to-back scheduled/dispatched GitHub Actions runs (`run 45093811570` `0.ofcas2dn1itq` and `run 45094311801` `0.ofcawbsajse8`).
4. ✅ **Met — The check's failure surfaces independently.** Scheduled GitHub Actions workflow [`alert-delivery-check.yml`](../.github/workflows/alert-delivery-check.yml) (`google_service_account.alert_verifier` keyless OIDC WIF in [`wif.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/wif.tf), using none of the channels it tests) surfaced an independent `FAIL` in `run 45086730009` (`2026-11-23T00:05:37Z`, single-batch Pub/Sub shard starvation behind 37 preserved operational messages) before passing end-to-end on `main` (`5fa41805`) in `run 45093811570` and `run 45094311801`.
5. ✅ **Met — Citation corrections.** Every `2026-11-16` `POAM-2026-230` note across `docs/`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `compliance/oscal/`, and `evidence_claim_census.jsonl` (`#862` `5fa41805`, `213` census entries, `0` errors across `US_FED`/`EU_ECB`/`APAC_MAS`), the Terraform `documentation` strings (`#859` `fc0152a8`), [`lula-validation-ir6.yaml`](../compliance/lula/lula-validation-ir6.yaml) L21 & L46 (`#859` `fc0152a8`), and the `v4.1.0` GitHub release body (`2026-11-22` maintainer edit matching `CHANGELOG.md`) state the verified Pub/Sub boundary and adopter-operated human fan-out.
6. ✅ **Met — Incident read-back.** Recorded below (`35`-message non-destructive Pub/Sub read-back on `cage-staging` + destroyed ephemeral Gate W project status).
7. ✅ **Met — Adopter-facing alert-stability invariants (folded in `2026-11-22` from queue read-back — Findings A & B).**
   - **Finding A (No orphaned pod-scoped incidents):** Pod-level threshold/absence conditions (`lula_audit_pod_restart` and `gateway_canary_pod_health`) aggregate across pod series (`cross_series_reducer = "REDUCE_SUM"` on `restart_count`, `"REDUCE_MAX"` on `uptime`) and all `9` `google_monitoring_alert_policy` resources set `alert_strategy { auto_close = "1800s" }` — verified live during the `fc0152a8` rollout when `gateway_canary_pod_health` incident `0.ofbqxms0ka30` opened at `2026-11-22T23:16:27Z` and auto-closed `124s` later at `23:18:31Z`.
   - **Finding B (Single-replica rolling-deploy turnover tolerance):** `prometheus_metrics_scrape_liveness` (`AU-12` Managed Prometheus operational telemetry scrape) aggregates `up` across replicas via `max by (job, namespace) (up{...}) == 0`, widens `absent_over_time` lookback from `[5m]` to `[10m]`, and sets `duration = "600s"` — verified live during the `fc0152a8` rollout (`0` `AU-12` scrape-liveness alerts fired vs. `24` across the 6 prior deploys).

**Citation sweep (`2026-11-16`, re-verified & updated `2026-11-23` in `#862` `5fa41805`):** Searched `docs/**`, `compliance/**`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md`, the Terraform comments and alert `documentation` strings, the Gate W certification record, and the GitHub release bodies published on or after `2026-11-09` (`v4.1.0`, `client-v0.3.0`, `conformance-v0.4.1`, `gate-w-8956f505`; read only) for the eight policy names, both variables, "alert policy", "page", "paging", "notify", "on-call", "alarm" and "dead-man". Originally corrected on `2026-11-16` with dated notes and updated on `2026-11-23` (`#862` `5fa41805` + `v4.1.0` release-body edit) to name the verified Pub/Sub terminal sink and adopter-operated human fan-out:

|---|---|---|
