### POAM-2026-231: The `#746` Canary and Gated-Request Metrics Are Biased Toward Healthy, and the Canary Cannot Boot on an Enforcing Deployment

**Control:** NIST SI-4 (System Monitoring), AU-5 (Response to Audit Logging Process Failures), CA-7 (Continuous Monitoring), SA-11 (Developer Testing and Evaluation)
**Risk Level:** Moderate (basis below)
**Status:** Open
**Owner:** Maintainer (gateway metrics and `infra/targets/gcp-gke` canary)
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-16
**Target Closure:** 2026-12-15

**Description:**
`#746` (`f0ca9f4d`, `2026-11-14`) added two outage alarms and a synthetic canary. [`WorkloadIdentityMiddleware`](../src/gateway/server/workload_identity.py) classifies each gated request as `blocked` when the response status is `>= 400` or the request was marked refused, and `permitted` otherwise (L530–535), and `gated_request_completed()` counts canary requests in both `cage_gateway_gated_requests_total` and `cage_gateway_canary_requests_total` ([`metrics.py`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/metrics.py) L180–194). The finance canary posts `market_analysis` to `/governance/validate-action` once every 60 seconds ([`plugin.py`](../src/cage_finance/plugin.py) L124–128; `gateway_canary_interval_seconds` default `60`, [`variables.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/variables.tf) L1461–1466). The alarms read those counters ([`metrics_alerting.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/metrics_alerting.tf)): the sustained refusal ratio is `blocked / total >= 0.95` over 5 minutes with at least 5 requests (L49–56), and zero-permitted needs `rate(permitted) == 0` while canary traffic is `> 0` (L60–64).

**Finding 1: one mechanism with three effects, whenever the probe is admitted.** Under hard denial (`403` or `503`, the probe included) the probe is refused, counts `blocked`, and zero-permitted works as designed. The three effects below hold only while the gateway admits the probe:
- **(a) Parking masks a total outage.** When the gateway parks every request as DEFER or REQUIRE_APPROVAL, the canary's own HTTP `200` DEFER counts `permitted`, so `rate(permitted) > 0` and `gateway_zero_permitted_requests` cannot fire.
- **(b) The canary raises the refusal-ratio trigger.** About five permitted probes per 5 minutes make the ratio `blocked / (blocked + 5)`, which reaches `0.95` only at `95` blocked requests in 5 minutes, instead of `5`.
- **(c) The client probe checks nothing.** [`run_canary_probe_once()`](../src/gateway/canary.py) reads `body["payload"]["governance"]["verdict"]` on the validate-action route (L104–106). The gateway's HTTP `200` envelope carries the verdict at `payload.verdict` ([`governance_middleware.py`](../src/gateway/server/governance_middleware.py) L1024–1033; [`governance_envelope.py`](../src/gateway/governance/governance_envelope.py) L375), so the read yields `None` and `verdict in ("ALLOW", None)` passes every HTTP `200`, DEFER and REQUIRE_APPROVAL included. A body of `{"payload": null}` raises `AttributeError` inside the probe. [`run_canary_loop()`](../src/gateway/canary.py) discards the result (L166).

**Finding 2: real traffic is biased the same way.** `handle_require_approval()` and `handle_defer()` ([`verdicts.py`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/verdicts.py) L602–672 and L675–737) return HTTP `200` verdicts without calling `mark_request_refused()`; its callers are `refusal_decided()` ([`metrics.py`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/metrics.py) L176), [`governance_middleware.py`](../src/gateway/server/governance_middleware.py) L874 and [`mcp_tool_server.py`](../src/gateway/server/mcp_tool_server.py). OPA `MANUAL_REVIEW` becomes REQUIRE_APPROVAL ([`classification_engine.py`](../src/gateway/governance/classification_engine.py) L174–175). So every DEFER, REQUIRE_APPROVAL and MANUAL_REVIEW request counts `permitted`: that causes effect (a) and understates the refusal ratio. Both `#746` metrics are biased in the same direction, toward looking healthy. The 2026-11-16 typed-outcome audit raised these as its rows F-10 and F-11; that audit is not a repository artifact, its row numbers are unrelated to the `F-` labels of `POAM-2026-189` to `POAM-2026-197`, and every claim here is cited to code.

**Finding 3: the canary cannot boot on an enforcing deployment.** `#764` (`3347b4b1`, `2026-11-15`) made `resolve_deployment_region()` raise `DeploymentRegionError` when `CAGE_DEPLOYMENT_REGION` is unset under an enforcing posture. The gateway, compliance bridge, advisor and reconciliation worker read it from the `cage-deployment` ConfigMap ([`gateway/main.tf`](../infra/modules/gateway/main.tf) L303–307, [`compliance_bridge/main.tf`](../infra/modules/compliance_bridge/main.tf) L156–160, [`governed_advisor/main.tf`](../infra/modules/governed_advisor/main.tf) L89–93, [`reconciliation_worker/main.tf`](../infra/modules/reconciliation_worker/main.tf) L199–203), whose module says to pass it to every workload ([`deployment_config/outputs.tf`](../infra/modules/deployment_config/outputs.tf) L16). [`gateway_canary.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/gateway_canary.tf) sets `CAGE_ENV` (L119) but not the region, and no test checks that boot contract across workload manifests: the canary tftest asserts that the Deployment is planned ([`lula_cron.tftest.hcl`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/tests/lula_cron.tftest.hcl) L175), not that it can start. So the canary crash-loops on every enforcing deployment of `main` since `#764`. Neither Gate W run had a canary: `8956f505` (`2026-11-13`) and `fa772122` (`2026-11-12`) both predate `#746`.

**Finding 4: probe coverage gap — single read-only probe stays green while mutating/CBF governance paths are wedged (realised live `2026-11-19`, independently corroborated by Cloud Monitoring delivery logs `2026-11-22`).** Even after the canary boots and checks `payload.verdict == "ALLOW"`, [`plugin.py`](../src/cage_finance/plugin.py) probes only read-only `market_analysis`. During the live `POAM-2026-238` outage on `cage-staging` (`2026-11-19T16:08:53Z`–`16:09:00Z`, `2c2cae96`), `reconciliation-worker` restarted at `sequence = 4 < last_accepted = 585`, wedging `100%` of `execute_trade` calls into HTTP `403` `CBF_RECONCILED_BALANCE_SEQUENCE_REPLAY_DETECTED` while `gateway-canary` continuously reported `200 OK` every 60s. **Independent delivery-log corroboration (`2026-11-22`, `POAM-2026-230`):** non-destructive read-back of all `35` messages in `subscriptions/cage-staging-alerts-verify` confirmed that `cage-staging-alerts-pubsub` was bound to all eight Cloud Monitoring policies at **`2026-11-19T16:07:46Z`** — **67 seconds before** `seq=2187..2191` wedged `execute_trade` (`16:08:53Z`–`16:09:00Z`) — yet `gateway_sustained_refusal_ratio` emitted **zero** notifications (`2` blocked `execute_trade` attempts stayed below the `5`-request volume floor while `~5` permitted `market_analysis` canary probes per 5 minutes diluted the denominator, raising the `>= 0.95` threshold to `95` blocked requests). That establishes on live telemetry and live alert delivery, not only by counter arithmetic, that a total mutating-tier wedge occurred in front of an active, wired refusal-ratio alarm without tripping it. Because `market_analysis` skips CBF ground-truth reconciliation, sequence validation, fiscal-limit reservation, and mutating-tier STPA/OPA rules, a green canary made a broader system-health claim than it tested. The coverage specification must therefore be defined by **which failure modes must turn the canary red** (not merely by enumerating a fixed list of action classes), so future governed actions and new governance stages have a clear rule for whether the canary probe suite must be extended.

**Operator episode (`2026-11-16`, recorded without assigning blame):** The staging canary was scaled to `0` at about 22:39Z on a premise later corrected, and restored to `1` at about 23:20Z. The canary has not completed a probe on `cage-staging` (`POAM-2026-230`, Realised), so neither change altered what any alarm could see: zero-permitted needs canary traffic, and there was none in either state. Scaling to `0` would have disabled that alarm, not unsuppressed it, had the canary been running, and no notification channel existed in either state (`POAM-2026-230`). The scale-down decision and the trade-off analysis that followed were made without checking that the canary pod was running; its `0/1` ready status was in the command output at the 22:39Z scale-down and was missed by both the maintainer and the agent. The analysis of what the control detects ran for four exchanges before anyone established that the control ran, which is the failure this register catalogues. The rule it implies: establish that a control is deployed and running (ready replicas, last successful run, policy enabled and bound) before reasoning about what it detects.

**Windows:** The defect window for findings 1 and 2 opens with `#746` (`f0ca9f4d`, `2026-11-14`), which added the alarms, the canary and the outcome counter, and covers every enforcing committed profile, `prod` included. Finding 3 opens with `#764` (`3347b4b1`, `2026-11-15`). Finding 4 opens with `#746` (`f0ca9f4d`, `2026-11-14`) and was realised live on `cage-staging` on `2026-11-19` during `POAM-2026-238`. The impact window is `cage-staging`, synthetic traffic only (no production deployment exists). There the canary had not run prior to the `CAGE_DEPLOYMENT_REGION` fix, so effects (a) to (c) were not realised on `2026-11-16`; what was realised on `2026-11-16` was finding 3 itself, which left zero-permitted with no canary traffic to condition on, and finding 2's count of parked staging requests as `permitted`, followed on `2026-11-19` by finding 4 while `execute_trade` was wedged behind `POAM-2026-238`. Independently, alert silence on `cage-staging` on `2026-11-16` involved two separate failures in the alarm path: every Cloud Monitoring alert policy had zero notification channels (`POAM-2026-230`), and compliance-bridge restarts (`15:01Z`, `15:28Z`, `18:10Z`) reset `_DEPLOYMENT_START_UTC` and re-armed the 6h `STARTUP_GRACE_HOURS` window across 9h (`15:01Z`–`00:12Z`), silencing `_check_lula_audit_deadman()` while `lula-audit` failed every run (`POAM-2026-234`), so even a wired channel would not have paged.

**Severity basis:** Moderate on both windows. Enforcement is unaffected: a parked request executes nothing until approved, and refusals still refuse. What is lost is detection, as in `POAM-2026-222` and `POAM-2026-230` (Moderate): an outage in which the gateway parks everything is invisible to both alarms, a refusal flood must be 19 times larger to trip the ratio, the canary meant to separate an idle cluster from a dead one could not boot prior to the region fix, and a single read-only probe remains green across a complete mutating/CBF wedge. It is not rated with `POAM-2026-221` (High) because nothing here reports a check green that ran no check; the alarms evaluate real counters that classify parking as success or probe only a read-only subset of the governance pipeline.

**Dependencies:** `POAM-2026-230` (**closed `2026-11-23`** via `#859` `fc0152a8` + `#862` `5fa41805`): routing prerequisite satisfied — all Cloud Monitoring policies now bind verified GCP Cloud Pub/Sub terminal delivery (`topics/cage-staging-alerts` → `subscriptions/cage-staging-alerts-verify`; downstream human paging fan-out is adopter-operated). `POAM-2026-233` (OPA outages signed as refusals) inflates the same refusal ratio from the other side, so the ratio is closed against both. `POAM-2026-234` tracks the broader favourable-error pattern across all measurement surfaces.

**Citation sweep (`2026-11-16`):** [`GATEWAY_ARCHITECTURE.md`](architecture/GATEWAY_ARCHITECTURE.md) L481 and L486 and [`GKE_TEST_RUNBOOK.md`](operations/GKE_TEST_RUNBOOK.md) L142 carry dated notes, and `POAM-2026-227` (closed) carries a dated correction. Cited, not edited, because they are Terraform: the [`metrics_alerting.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/metrics_alerting.tf) comments and `documentation` strings that describe the canary as separating an idle cluster from an outage (L57–59, L167–179, L263–273), and the `enable_gateway_canary` description in [`variables.tf`](../infra/targets/gcp-gke/variables.tf) (L1455). No OSCAL statement, census row or Lula manifest makes a canary or refusal-ratio liveness claim.

**Remediation:** a separate PR adds the region from the `cage-deployment` ConfigMap to the canary and a test that enumerates every workload manifest; the metric, client, and failure-mode probe-coverage changes follow the closure criteria.

**Closure Criteria:**
1. DEFER, REQUIRE_APPROVAL and MANUAL_REVIEW carry their own outcome label, never `permitted`.
2. The client checks `payload.verdict == "ALLOW"` strictly, records a probe-outcome metric, handles a malformed body as a failed probe, and does not discard results.
3. The refusal ratio is computed over non-canary traffic.
4. A planted DEFER-parking test proves `gateway_zero_permitted_requests` fires.
5. A test enumerates every workload manifest and fails when one omits the region its posture requires, and the canary is read back on staging completing probes.
6. **Failure-mode coverage contract:** the canary specification explicitly defines **which governance-pipeline failure modes must turn the canary red** — at minimum: (a) policy-engine (`OPA`) outage or malformed decision document, (b) server-input feed / market-data / NAV outage, (c) `CBF` ground-truth snapshot absence, staleness, KMS-signature invalidity, or reconciliation sequence regression (the `POAM-2026-238` wedge), (d) `DB 0` fiscal/CBF store or `DB 1` `DeferQueue`/evidence-stream unavailability, and (e) universal `DEFER`/`REQUIRE_APPROVAL` parking — and maps each required failure mode to an explicit side-effect-free probe (for example, read-only `market_analysis` plus a dry-run/preview CBF-gated mutating check that exercises reconciliation sequence verification without mutating live ledger state). A planted-failure test for each listed failure mode proves the canary turns red, and adding a governed action that introduces a new required enforcement stage explicitly extends the failure-mode contract.

### POAM-2026-232: The UNKNOWN Actuation Lifecycle Is Broken at Four Stages: Classification, Fiscal Reclamation, Surfacing and Resubmission

**Control:** NIST SC-4 (fiscal limits, CAGE mapping), SC-24 (Fail in Known State), SI-10 (Information Input Validation), AU-10 (Non-repudiation), SA-8 (Security and Privacy Engineering Principles)
**Risk Level:** High (basis below)
**Status:** Open
**Owner:** Maintainer (actuation seam, finance domain and advisor)
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-16
**Target Closure:** 2026-12-15

**Description:**
An actuation whose outcome is unknown (the order may have filled) has to be classified UNKNOWN, kept reserved until a broker lookup settles it, reported as indeterminate, and never resubmitted under a new idempotency key. All four stages were broken at `c5de2555` (`2026-11-16` typed-outcome audit rows F-06, F-21 and F-29 to F-34; not a repository artifact, every claim below is cited to code); `#797` (`3dfb453d`) and `#801` (`f58592ec`) closed the core Stage 1 seam on `2026-11-17`, activating Stage 2.

**Stage 1: classification.**
- **Prior to `2026-11-17`, a post-dispatch broker failure settled REJECTED.** At `c5de2555`, [`trade_executor.py`](../src/cage_finance/tools/trade_executor.py) turned any exception after the order POST, a timeout or `5xx` included, into `RuntimeError` (`c5de2555^:src/cage_finance/tools/trade_executor.py` L143–172), and [`broker_actuator.py`](../src/cage_finance/actuators/broker_actuator.py) returned a receipt with `accepted=False`, no `outcome` and `retryable=True` (`c5de2555^:src/cage_finance/actuators/broker_actuator.py` L362–378). [`ActuationReceipt`](../src/gateway/governance/seams/actuation.py) then derived REJECTED from `accepted` (`c5de2555^:src/gateway/governance/seams/actuation.py` L253–259), `may_have_executed` was `False` (L276–278), and the finance tool settled `executed=False` ([`tool_provider.py`](../src/cage_finance/tools/tool_provider.py) L517, L537–538), releasing the CBF and fiscal reservations of an order that may have filled.
- **Prior to `2026-11-17`, cancellation during dispatch left no receipt and healthcare reported UNKNOWN as BLOCKED.** `dispatch_actuation()` caught only `Exception` (`c5de2555^:src/gateway/governance/execution_actuator.py` L82–105), so a `CancelledError` skipped the receipt and its evidence, and a non-accepted healthcare receipt returned a signed refusal while `executed` was `True` (`c5de2555^:src/cage_healthcare/tools/tool_provider.py` L123–125; a non-production reference domain).
- **Landed `2026-11-17` (`#797` `3dfb453d`, `#801` `f58592ec`):** `ActuationReceipt.outcome` is now a required keyword-only field with no default (`DA-01`), [`trade_executor.py`](../src/cage_finance/tools/trade_executor.py) tracks wire dispatch structurally (`DispatchPhase`) and settles post-wire failures and duplicate-id `422`s as `UNKNOWN` (and requires an explicit terminal fill status on `2xx`), [`dispatch_actuation()`](../src/gateway/governance/execution_actuator.py) shields an `ACTUATION_INDETERMINATE_RECEIPT` (`outcome=UNKNOWN`) before re-raising `asyncio.CancelledError` (`F-30`), and [`cage_healthcare/tools/tool_provider.py`](../src/cage_healthcare/tools/tool_provider.py) returns `status == "INDETERMINATE"` without signing a false refusal (`F-31`).
- **Still open in Stage 1 — partner mapping by status alone.** `actuator_02` treats `{400, 401, 403, 409, 421, 422, 429, 503}` as definitive refusals ([`adapter.py`](../src/integrations/actuator_02/adapter.py) L86–88), and the `actuator_01` classifier accepts any HTTP `200` carrying a `receipt_id` ([`response_classifier.py`](../src/integrations/actuator_01/response_classifier.py) L227–256). Per the audit, the two partner adapters refuse the domain executor ids and so affect adopters rather than the reference trade path; that reachability note is not re-verified here.

**Stage 2: fiscal reclamation (activated by `DA-01` landing on `2026-11-17`).** With `DA-01` merged (`3dfb453d`), post-wire failures now settle `UNKNOWN` with `executed=True` ([`tool_provider.py`](../src/cage_finance/tools/tool_provider.py) L531–545), which confirms the reservation: [`FiscalLimitGuard.confirm()`](../src/cage_finance/safety/fiscal_limit_guard.py) makes it permanent within the active window, so the amount counts against the daily limit whether or not the order filled. **Daily-reset bound (`<= 24h`, non-cumulative):** [`FiscalLimitGuard._window_key()`](../src/cage_finance/safety/fiscal_limit_guard.py) (L222–224) keys spend to `fiscal:daily_limit:%Y-%m-%d` (`time.gmtime()`), rotating cleanly at `00:00Z`. An unreclaimed `UNKNOWN` actuation therefore locks fiscal capacity for **at most the remainder of that UTC calendar day (`<= 24h`) per incident**, never cumulatively across days. Within that day, nothing reconciles fiscal spend against broker fills (the reconciliation daemon has no fiscal path, and `reclaim_expired()` releases only reservations that were never settled, L250–264), and nothing alarms on a confirmed-but-unverified amount, while CBF debits drain through reconciliation snapshots ([`daemon.py`](../src/gateway/governance/reconciliation/daemon.py) L1035–1045). Holding the money for the remainder of the UTC day is the safe fail-closed direction; holding it without a same-day resolution path or alarm is the remaining Stage 2 gap.

**Stage 3: surfacing.** At `c5de2555`, `/tools/execute` returned HTTP `200` with `{"status": "SUCCESS", "output": str(output)}` or `{"status": "ERROR", "error": str(exc)}` while finance raised the same `SymbolicGovernorViolation` for rejected and indeterminate outcomes. `#789` (`127eebc2`) and `#797` (`3dfb453d`) added `ActuationIndeterminateError` (subclassing `SymbolicGovernorViolation`) on finance and `error_type` on `/tools/execute` HTTP `200` `status: "ERROR"` responses (preventing generic HTTP `500` flattening), but domain-agnostic seam exception types (`ActuationRejectedError` vs. `ActuationIndeterminateError`) and distinct non-refusal gated-request accounting (`mcp_tool_server.py` still marks `SymbolicGovernorViolation` subclasses refused) remain open.

**Stage 4: resubmission safety.** When the MCP client loses contact after sending `tools/call`, `_call_tool_at_most_once()` raises `MCPToolOutcomeUnknownError` ([`mcp_client.py`](../src/gateway/infrastructure/mcp_client.py) L435–481), and `/tools/execute` errors return text into the advisor. Inside the trader subgraph, `tool_executor_node()` catches `except Exception` and emits a `ToolMessage("Error executing tool ...")` ([`governed_trader_graph.py`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/subgraphs/governed_trader_graph.py) L194–201). `gateway_tool_guard()` unconditionally returns `governance_status = GOVERNANCE_ALLOWED` after `func()` returns regardless of tool outcome ([`tool_guard.py`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/governance/tool_guard.py) L276–283, L374–380), and `route_after_tools()` loops back to `"executor"` on `GOVERNANCE_ALLOWED` ([`governed_trader_graph.py`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/subgraphs/governed_trader_graph.py) L289–295). If the executor LLM re-proposes the trade, the new `tool_call` has a new `tool_call_id`; `derive_transaction_id()` hashes `tool_call_id` rather than plan step or intent ([`tool_guard.py`](../src/governed_financial_advisor/graph/governance/tool_guard.py) L167–175), so the retry receives a fresh `transaction_id` and bypasses the gateway's execution-idempotency ledger (`UnsettledDuplicate`). Whether any specific model currently chooses to re-propose is beside the point: double-execution safety cannot rely on an LLM deciding not to retry after an indeterminate error.

**Dependencies & sequencing:** `DA-01` (`#797`, `3dfb453d`) and `F-30` (`#801`, `f58592ec`) landed on `2026-11-17`, activating Stage 2 (`UNKNOWN` outcomes now hold daily fiscal capacity rather than releasing on post-wire failure). Because `FiscalLimitGuard._window_key()` bounds any unreclaimed `UNKNOWN` hold to at most one UTC calendar day (`<= 24h`) per incident, **`POAM-2026-233` (structural false KMS-signed policy refusals) remains sequenced ahead of this item**. `POAM-2026-230` (**closed `2026-11-23`** via `#859` `fc0152a8` + `#862` `5fa41805`) satisfies the alert-routing prerequisite so the unresolved-`UNKNOWN` alarm required by Closure Criterion 4 binds CAGE's verified Pub/Sub terminal sink (`topics/cage-staging-alerts` → `subscriptions/cage-staging-alerts-verify`).

**Windows:** The defect window opens with the finance actuator and fiscal guard introduction (`#110` `f8ec5151` and `#114` `8309d854`, `2026-08-31`; `ActuationOutcome` in `#391` `e1f46eca`, `2026-10-04`; `UnsettledDuplicate` in `#528` `f565e4ed`, `2026-10-24`) and applies to every committed deployment profile. The impact window is `cage-staging`, synthetic traffic only (no production deployment or live broker exists); read-back of all `27` entries in `cage:evidence:stream` on `2026-11-16` shows `0` `ACTUATION_INDETERMINATE_RECEIPT` records.

**Severity basis:** High on the defect window (the headline rating matches the Stage 4 fresh-key retry double-execution path and partner Stage 1 classifiers on any live broker deployment, while explicitly scoping the impact window to staging synthetic traffic only). Stage 1's core `DA-01` omission defect is closed (`3dfb453d`); Stage 2's unreclaimed hold is fail-closed and bounded to `<= 24h` (`00:00Z` UTC key rotation), not an unbounded lockout; Stage 4 still allows an LLM retry under a fresh idempotency key after an indeterminate failure.

**Citation sweep (`2026-11-16`):** Searched `docs/`, `compliance/oscal/`, and `compliance/lula/` for `ACTUATION_INDETERMINATE`, `FiscalLimitGuard.confirm`, `may_have_executed`, and `UnsettledDuplicate`. No OSCAL statement, census row, or Lula manifest claims broker-side fiscal reclamation or post-UNKNOWN retry blocking; [`docs/BREAKING_CHANGES.md`](BREAKING_CHANGES.md) records `DA-01` (`#797`, `3dfb453d`).

**Remediation:**
1. Complete remaining Stage 1 partner adapter status classifiers (`actuator_01` and `actuator_02`; core `DA-01` seam, `trade_executor`, `CancelledError` receipting, and healthcare `INDETERMINATE` landed in `#797` `3dfb453d` and `#801` `f58592ec`).
2. Add broker-order lookup / reconciliation for confirmed-but-unverified fiscal reservations within the active `fiscal:daily_limit:%Y-%m-%d` UTC window (releasing confirmed spend when broker lookup proves non-execution, keeping it when filled, and alarming on aged unresolved `UNKNOWN` reservations).
3. Surface `REJECTED`, `UNKNOWN`, and `UnsettledDuplicate` as distinct domain-agnostic typed outcomes across `src/gateway/governance/seams/actuation.py`, `mcp_tool_server.py` (without counting indeterminate fills as policy refusals), and the advisor client.
4. Stop the advisor trader subgraph on any indeterminate actuation outcome (do not set `GOVERNANCE_ALLOWED` and loop back to the LLM) and bind `transaction_id` to the approved plan step/intent rather than a per-LLM-call `tool_call_id`.

**Closure Criteria:**
1. Every stage above is fixed on `main`: `ActuationReceipt.outcome` is required with no default (`3dfb453d`); post-wire ambiguity and cancellation settle `UNKNOWN` with evidence (`3dfb453d`, `f58592ec`); partner classifiers no longer infer non-execution from ambiguous statuses; `REJECTED`, `UNKNOWN`, and `UnsettledDuplicate` carry distinct typed outcomes through `/tools/execute` to the advisor; and an indeterminate tool outcome terminates the trader subgraph rather than looping to the LLM under a new `tool_call_id`.
2. Confirmed fiscal reservations from `UNKNOWN` actuations have a reconciliation/reclamation path backed by broker lookup (or documented operator settlement) so non-executed `UNKNOWN` attempts do not hold capacity for the remainder of the UTC calendar day (`<= 24h`) without a resolution path.
3. One end-to-end test drives a single trade through all four stages: broker timeout -> `UNKNOWN` classification + evidence + reservation held -> typed indeterminate surfacing -> advisor halt without fresh-key resubmission -> broker lookup settlement reclaiming (on non-fill) or finalizing (on fill) fiscal capacity.
4. An alert fires on aged unresolved `UNKNOWN` actuations and is bound to a verified notification channel per `POAM-2026-230`.

### POAM-2026-233: Infrastructure Failures Are Recorded and Signed as Policy Refusals (False Attestation)

**Control:** NIST AU-10 (Non-repudiation), AU-3 (Content of Audit Records), SI-11 (Error Handling), SC-24 (Fail in Known State), AC-3 (Access Enforcement), SI-4 (System Monitoring)
**Risk Level:** High (proposed; defect and impact windows under **Severity** below)
**Status:** Open
**Owner:** Maintainer
**Date Opened:** 2026-11-16
**Target Closure:** 2026-11-30

**Description:**
Blocking a request when a dependency fails is correct and must stay fail-closed. The defect is how the block is recorded: as a policy decision. The gateway writes an immutable, citable refusal record, signed and counted like any other, asserting that a policy refused an action when no policy decided anything. This happens structurally, on every occurrence, not by accident. The design treats refusals as primary evidence ([`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md), "Refusals Are Primary Evidence"), so the false record is the authoritative one. Line numbers below are `c5de2555`.

**Causes.** Each is an infrastructure or configuration failure that enters the governor as a HARD violation:
1. **OPA (audit row F-01; core taxonomy remediated in PR 1 `FA-1`).** Prior to `FA-1`, `evaluate_policy()` (`c5de2555^:src/gateway/core/policy.py` lines 657-661, 668-674, 680-685) returned `"DENY"` when the latency budget was exhausted, when the circuit breaker was open, and on any unexpected exception. `_query_opa()` (`c5de2555^:src/gateway/core/policy.py` lines 734-780) sent pool timeout, protocol error, transport error or timeout, any other exception, HTTP `5xx`/`408`/`429`, other non-2xx and a malformed body through `_deny()` (`c5de2555^:src/gateway/core/policy.py` lines 463-470), whose docstring read "the decision is always DENY". A `200` reply without a `result` (an undefined decision document) also became `DENY` (`c5de2555^:src/gateway/core/policy.py` line 782) and logged no failure at all. The kernel contract required this: `PolicyClient` (`c5de2555^:src/gateway/governance/contracts.py` lines 1287-1290) said "Implementations fail closed: an unreachable or erroring policy engine yields `"DENY"`", and its `str` return had no unavailable value. `OpaStage` (`c5de2555^:src/gateway/governance/governor/stages/opa.py` lines 100-114) emitted `OPA_ERROR` only when the client raised, which a conforming client never did, so every failure became `OPA_DENY` (`_violations_for()` in `c5de2555^:src/gateway/governance/governor/stages/opa.py` lines 126-134, HARD, "OPA Denied Action.").
2. **Server inputs (F-02; source outages remediated in `#817` `2c2cae96` `FA-2`, rule-body `except` blocks open).** Prior to `FA-2`, [`bind_server_inputs()`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/server_inputs.py) left owned keys unset whenever a resolver raised, and [`trade_inputs.py`](../src/cage_finance/tools/trade_inputs.py) dropped missing or timed-out feeds so UCA-2 / UCA-5 / UCA-6 / UCA-13 refused absent inputs under the breach's own code (`STPA_UCA_UCA_2`, `STPA_UCA_UCA_5`, `STPA_UCA_UCA_6`, `STPA_UCA_UCA_13` in [`uca_rules.py`](../src/cage_finance/stpa/uca_rules.py)). `#817` (`2c2cae96`, `FA-2`) introduces [`ServerInputUnavailableError`](../src/gateway/governance/contracts.py) and [`TradeInputSourceUnavailable`](../src/cage_finance/tools/trade_inputs.py) so `market_data`, `portfolio_nav`, and `trader_identity` source outages fail closed with `503` `server_input_unavailable` (preserving post-HITL approvals), while present readings that fail validation (`STALE_TIMESTAMP`, `FUTURE_TIMESTAMP`, `NAN_VALUE`, `NEGATIVE_VALUE`, `MALFORMED_PAYLOAD`, `UNVERIFIED_SOURCE`) and missing caller identity (`TraderIdentityUnavailable`) continue to refuse as `ViolationKind.HARD`. Rule-body `except Exception` handlers in [`stpa_validator.py`](../src/gateway/governance/stpa_validator.py) (`L149`) and generated [`uca_rules.py`](../src/cage_finance/stpa/uca_rules.py) remain open in `POAM-2026-233`.
3. **DeferQueue and execution ledger (F-03; remediated in `#817` `2c2cae96` `FA-2`).** Prior to `FA-2`, in [`enforce_approved_governance()`](../src/gateway/server/governance_middleware.py) a `DeferQueue` exception while checking an approval became an `AC-3` refusal ("no unconsumed approval ... covers this"), while a Redis failure inside [`DeferQueue._atomic_resolve()`](../src/gateway/governance/defer_queue.py) (`c0d9b6fd^:src/gateway/governance/defer_queue.py` L1242-1249) or `consume_approval()` returned `False` (`# treat errors as "already resolved"`) and fabricated `APPROVAL_NOT_REDEEMABLE` ("already spent, expired or no longer covers the request"). Likewise, `ExecutionLedgerUnavailable` emitted an `AC-3` `record_refusal()` (`c0d9b6fd^:src/cage_finance/tools/tool_provider.py` L247-256) and `503` blocks after `ledger.claim()` poisoned the `transaction_id` as `BLOCKED`. `#817` (`2c2cae96`, `FA-2`) propagates Redis errors from `_atomic_resolve(..., raise_on_error=True)` into [`ApprovalSpendUnavailableError`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/errors.py), rolls back Phase-2 reservations LIFO while keeping the token `RESOLVED` (`503` `defer_queue_unavailable`), routes `ExecutionLedgerUnavailable` to `503` `execution_ledger_unavailable`, releases unexecuted `IN_FLIGHT` claims via [`ExecutionLedger.release_unexecuted()`](../src/gateway/governance/execution_idempotency.py), and removes `mark_request_refused()` from `EvidenceChainUnavailableError` in [`mcp_tool_server.py`](../src/gateway/server/mcp_tool_server.py).
4. **Causal telemetry (found by the enumeration below; remains open).** The optional finance causal tier answers a telemetry-provider failure, or the absence of live telemetry in an enforcing posture, with HARD `CAUSAL_TELEMETRY_UNAVAILABLE` ([`CausalTierPlugin`](../src/cage_finance/tiers/causal_tier.py) lines 196-201, 216-221). The code is accurate; the record class is a refusal.
5. **Consensus configuration (found by the enumeration; remains open).** [`check_consensus()`](../src/gateway/governance/consensus/engine.py) lines 594-625 returns `DENY` when no inference backend is configured (`CONSENSUS_NO_INFERENCE_BACKEND`) or no critics are configured, and the consensus tier records it as a HARD refusal.
6. **Stage exceptions, `CBF` / `FiscalLimitGuard` store & reconciliation outages, and `FTRA` boundary/registry unavailability (remediated in `#817` `2c2cae96` `FA-2`; residual `BoundingContractTierPlugin` / `FriaTierPlugin` `except` blocks open).** Prior to `FA-2`, unhandled stage/rollback exceptions (`TIER_EXCEPTION`, `STPA_ERROR`, `ROLLBACK_FAILED`, `CONFIRM_FAILED`), pure CBF store/reconciliation unavailability (`RECONCILIATION_UNAVAILABLE:` in [`cbf_engine.py`](../src/gateway/governance/safety/cbf_engine.py) and missing reconciler keys in `verify_action()`), `FiscalLimitGuard` Redis Lua/read errors (`result = -2` / `None` in [`fiscal_limit_guard.py`](../src/cage_finance/safety/fiscal_limit_guard.py)), and `FTRA` analyzer exceptions or unreadable registries (`FTRA_ERROR` in [`ftra.py`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/stages/ftra.py), `FTRA_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE` in [`ftra/models.py`](../src/gateway/governance/ftra/models.py)) all entered the governor as `ViolationKind.HARD`. `#817` (`2c2cae96`, `FA-2`) reclassifies each of those pure dependency outages as `ViolationKind.INFRASTRUCTURE` (`CBF_RECONCILIATION_UNAVAILABLE`, `FISCAL_STORE_UNAVAILABLE`, `TIER_EXCEPTION`, `STPA_ERROR`, `ROLLBACK_FAILED`, `FTRA_ERROR`, `FTRA_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE` with `classification="UNAVAILABLE"`, `irreversibility_score=None`, `bypassed_ftra_node=False`), while strictly preserving `ViolationKind.HARD` on active discrepancy fences (`RECONCILIATION_FENCE_ACTIVE`), fence epoch regressions, sequence regressions, unsigned production snapshots, KMS verification rejections, and genuine fiscal cap breaches (`FISCAL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`).

**Upstream `except` producers fabricating substantive policy claims (inverse AST audit, `2026-11-18`):**
- `DeferQueue._atomic_resolve` ([`defer_queue.py`](../src/gateway/governance/defer_queue.py)) / `enforce_approved_governance` ([`governance_middleware.py`](../src/gateway/server/governance_middleware.py)): signed `APPROVAL_NOT_REDEEMABLE` asserting replay, expiry, or non-coverage on `DB 1` Redis errors (**remediated in `#817` `2c2cae96` `FA-2`**).
- `ControlBarrierFunction` / `FiscalLimitGuard` / `_settle_each` ([`cbf_engine.py`](../src/gateway/governance/safety/cbf_engine.py), [`barrier_tier.py`](../src/gateway/governance/safety/barrier_tier.py), [`fiscal_limit_guard.py`](../src/cage_finance/safety/fiscal_limit_guard.py), [`reservation.py`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/reservation.py)): signed `APPROVAL_CONTEXT_DRIFT` and burned `DB 1` approvals on `DB 0` store/reconciliation or rollback outages (**remediated in `#817` `2c2cae96` `FA-2`**).
- `FtraStage._ftra_boundary_check` ([`ftra.py`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/stages/ftra.py)) and `FTRA_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE` ([`ftra/models.py`](../src/gateway/governance/ftra/models.py)): synthesized `IRREVERSIBLE_TERMINAL` (`irreversibility_score=1.0`, `bypassed_ftra_node=True`) + `HARD` `FTRA_ERROR` / `FTRA_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE` on analyzer exceptions or unreadable registries (**remediated in `#817` `2c2cae96` `FA-2`**).
- `bind_server_inputs` / `TradeInputResolver` ([`server_inputs.py`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/server_inputs.py), [`trade_inputs.py`](../src/cage_finance/tools/trade_inputs.py)) and `stpa_validator.py` / generated `uca_rules.py`: signed `STPA_UCA_*` asserting stale market data or excessive drawdown when no feed responded or a rule raised (**absent feeds remediated in `#817` `2c2cae96` `FA-2`**; `stpa_validator.py` L149 and generated `uca_rules.py` rule-body `except Exception` tracked in remaining `POAM-2026-233` scope).
- `contract_b10_rollback_window` ([`contracts.py`](../src/cage_finance/safety/bounding/contracts.py) L1377): calls `_b10_window_closed(..., 'Rollback capability provider unavailable')`, asserting the rollback window closed on a provider `RuntimeError`, while `B3`/`B5`/`B8` (`L513, 732, 927`) escalate dead feeds to `HITL_ESCALATE`, `B3`/`B5`/`B7`/`B8`/`B10` (`L499, 719, 913, 1221, 1363`) emit `HARD_BLOCK`, and `FriaTierPlugin._unavailable` ([`fria_tier.py`](../src/gateway/governance/jurisdiction/eu_ai_act/fria_tier.py) L212, 233, 237, 335) emits `FRIA_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` as `ViolationKind.HARD` (**catalogued in remaining `POAM-2026-233` scope**).

All six converge on one path. [`ClassificationEngine`](../src/gateway/governance/classification_engine.py) lines 138-140 maps any HARD finding to `DENY`. `_VERDICT_HANDLERS` sends `DENY` to `handle_deny()` ([`governor.py`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/governor.py) lines 1725-1731, with unmapped decisions also falling through to it at line 383). [`handle_deny()`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/verdicts.py) lines 836-878 builds the refusal receipt, increments `cage_governance_refusals_total` and hash-chains a `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL`. The middleware then KMS-signs a `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL_RECEIPT` ([`_emit_refusal_receipt()`](../src/gateway/server/governance_middleware.py) lines 729-760), and `validate-action` answers `403 DENIED` with `proof_hash` ([`validate_action_endpoint()`](../src/gateway/server/governance_middleware.py) lines 1073-1350). The same endpoint already answers a typed `503 evidence_chain_unavailable` when the evidence chain is down (lines 1104-1114); that is the shape the fix should follow.

**Defect window** (`git log -S` on `main`):
- OPA failures have returned `DENY` since the first commit, `1902c92c` (2026-06-01, `release: v2.0.0-dev.1`: the open-breaker, latency and failure paths of `evaluate_policy`).
- Every hard refusal has carried a KMS-signed refusal receipt since `c7174e05` (2026-06-06), whose `symbolic_governor.py` already turned an OPA `DENY` into "OPA Denied Action". The false, signed attestation has therefore been possible since 2026-06-06.
- The `OPA_ERROR` branch arrived in `5a1f9aa1` (`#265`, 2026-09-26) and has been unreachable for a conforming client since then.
- The `PolicyClient` sentence that mandates `DENY` arrived in `b4bb9ef7` (`#407`, 2026-10-06). The `_deny()` helper and its docstring arrived in `95df9460` (`#506`, 2026-10-22).
- Server-input binding that leaves owned keys unset arrived in `236dc9e9` (`#429`, 2026-10-06). The core STPA validator has kept the breach code on evaluation errors since `1902c92c`.
- The approval spend took its current form in `6f92eca4` (`#436`, 2026-10-07), which also added `APPROVAL_NOT_REDEEMABLE` and the DeferQueue-outage refusal. Its message records the rule: "A DENY still spends it ... No refund path exists." Before `#436` the gateway consumed the approval before re-validation ran (`POAM-2026-104` gap 3), so every refused or failed post-approval run burned it; `consume_approval` dates from `b722146a` (`#329`, 2026-10-01).
- The execution-ledger refusal arrived in `f565e4ed` (`#528`, 2026-10-24) and `cage_governance_refusals_total` in `99d0affd` (`#588`, 2026-10-29).
- **Auto-quarantine `startswith("FTRA")` / `startswith("RECON")` + `else: CRITICAL_CBF_BREACH` (row 10):** Opened `2026-10-04` in `dd8a2510` (`#393`, which introduced both `CAGE_ENABLE_AUTO_QUARANTINE` and caller-supplied `_quarantine_on_breach`). Caller-supplied `_quarantine_on_breach` was stripped and removed from `verdicts.py` on `2026-11-17` in `f32c0e5b` (`#798`), leaving only `CAGE_ENABLE_AUTO_QUARANTINE`; `#817` (`2c2cae96`, `FA-2`) replaces prefix and `else:` dispatch with `Violation.quarantine_trigger` + `_QUARANTINE_TRIGGER_BY_CODE`, gated across all `src/**/*.py` by [`check_violation_quarantine_ledger.py`](../scripts/check_violation_quarantine_ledger.py).

**Impact window.** No production deployment exists; `cage-staging` carries synthetic traffic only. Searched read-only on 2026-11-16 through `gcloud logging read` over the cluster's container logs in the default Cloud Logging bucket, whose 30-day retention leaves nothing before 2026-10-18T00:35Z; older logs are unavailable. Project identifiers are withheld (`<PROJECT_ID>`).
- **OPA (cause 1):** 9 `OPA FAILURE` lines, all `OPA FAILURE (UNEXPECTED_ERROR); denying.` from one gateway pod between 2026-10-25T12:48:20Z and 12:48:57Z. There were 0 breaker-open, fast-fail, latency-budget or half-open lines. Eight of the nine were followed within 3 ms by `handle_deny DENY: action=execute_trade` on `POST /governance/validate-action`. Their `exc_info` names the trigger: `TypeError: Cannot mutate immutable BoundedAttributes`, raised by the gateway's own span processor while the OPA span ended. Neither OPA nor any policy decided anything. By code path, each of those eight `handle_deny` calls incremented `cage_governance_refusals_total` and hash-chained a `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL` naming `OPA_DENY` before raising; no `Failed to publish refusal receipt` line was logged between 12:40Z and 13:00Z. A second `TypeError` at the `validate_action` span exit replaced the `GovernanceError`, so each request ended in `500`, not `403`, and no per-request `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL_RECEIPT` was signed. The trigger itself was fixed in `a2af1a01` (`#535`) the same day; the conversion that turned it into a policy refusal was not. The ninth line (12:48:57Z) had no `handle_deny` after it.
- **Causal telemetry (cause 4):** between 2026-10-22T13:24Z and 16:56Z `handle_deny` logged 396 refusals, and 689 exported span lines name `[CAUSAL_TELEMETRY_UNAVAILABLE]` as the `GovernanceError` raised from `handle_deny`. That is about 230 refusals at the three lines per refusal seen in the samples read.
- **Causes 2, 3 and 6:** 0 lines for `will refuse`, `owned keys stay unset`, `DeferQueue unavailable`, `execution ledger unavailable`, `could not spend approval`, `TIER_EXCEPTION` and `APPROVAL_NOT_REDEEMABLE`.
- **Evidence stream:** a read-only `XLEN`/`XRANGE` of `cage:evidence:stream` on 2026-11-16 found 27 entries, from 2026-11-09T04:50:57Z to 2026-11-16T19:30:34Z: 2 `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL`, 3 `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL_RECEIPT`, 0 naming `OPA_DENY`. The 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-25 records predate the earliest retained entry and cannot be read back.
- **Not countable from logs:** the undefined-decision path (cause 1) logs nothing, and a burned approval leaves no log line.
- **`CAGE_ENABLE_AUTO_QUARANTINE` (row 10): empty.** No committed Terraform module, `.tfvars` profile, Kubernetes manifest, Dockerfile, `.env`, or CI workflow sets `CAGE_ENABLE_AUTO_QUARANTINE` (`None` verified live on `cage-staging` on `2026-11-18`), and unlike `CAGE_ALLOW_ASSERTED_PRINCIPAL`, zero operator documentation mentions or recommends the flag.

**Published Gate W Certification Negative Result (`2026-11-16`):** Recomputing per-control metrics across all three published Gate W WORM certification archives (`8956f505`, `fa772122-clean-room`, and `fa772122-recovery`; see [`gate_w_certification.json`](../compliance/gate_w_certification.json)) confirmed `0` OPA-outage or infrastructure-failure refusals during any certification run, and excluding every refusal, deferral, refusal-receipt, and quarantine-block record leaves `safety_rate = 1.0000` across all five populated controls in `SUPPORTED_CONTROLS` (`A.5.2`, `A.5.3`, `A.8.4`, `A.9.2`, `SC-4`). Published Gate W certification archive verdicts were **not** contaminated by row 17 (`_is_control_effective_record()`); the structural defect remains live on `main` and is tracked jointly with `POAM-2026-234`.

**Severity (proposed High).** The defect window is structural and long: since 2026-06-06 for the signed OPA path, and since `#436` for the approval burn in its current form. The impact window is staging only, with synthetic traffic, and false refusals were realized twice in the 30 days that remain. Not Critical: blocking stayed fail-closed, no unsafe action was permitted, and no production record exists. Not Moderate (the `POAM-2026-228` rating): this corrupts the authoritative evidence itself (AU-10), on every occurrence, beyond correction once written (a record can only be annotated), and it destroys a human approval. An adopter carrying real traffic would hold false regulatory records and should rate it Critical.

**Consumers.** Every branch that reads the violation classification or a refusal it produces, found by the search under **Enumeration method**. Each row gives what the consumer does with a refusal, how an infrastructure-caused refusal corrupts it, and what the fix must do there.

| # | Consumer | What it does with a refusal | How a false refusal corrupts it | What the fix must do |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Classification ([`ClassificationEngine`](../src/gateway/governance/classification_engine.py) lines 138-140; [`governor.py`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/governor.py) lines 1725-1731, 385) | Maps any HARD finding to `DENY`; unmapped decisions fall through to `handle_deny` | A HARD finding has no route except a refusal | Give infrastructure blocks their own kind and outcome, routed to their own handler |
| 2 | Evidence writer ([`handle_deny()`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/verdicts.py) lines 836-878; [`publish_refusal()`](../src/gateway/governance/governor/verdicts.py) lines 145-190; [`_emit_refusal_receipt()`](../src/gateway/server/governance_middleware.py) lines 729-760) | Hash-chains `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL` (covered by the custodian's KMS-signed batch attestation) and KMS-signs `GOVERNANCE_REFUSAL_RECEIPT` | A signed, immutable record of a decision no policy made | Emit a distinct hash-chained infrastructure-block event naming the dependency; no `RefusalReceipt`, no `proof_hash` |
